entries.abstract: Whitehead's asphericity problem would have a negative answer if a non-aspherical two-complex began an infinite chain whose inclusions induce zero maps on second homotopy groups. This Lean formalization proves the article's main finite-length characterization: a connected two-complex K begins such chains of every finite length if and only if K has a connected acyclic regular cover. It also formalizes the finite acyclic enhancement.
entries.title: Finite Chains of Two-Complexes and Acyclic Covers

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the strict Neumann Pólya inequality for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains in the plane. The plane is identified with ℂ; the Neumann eigenvalues μ_0 ≤ μ_1 ≤ ... are defined by the Courant–Fischer min–max formula for the form ∫|∇u|² on H¹(Ω) (weak gradients in L²), indexed from 0 and repeated according to multiplicity, and N_N(E) = #{j ≥ 0 : μ_j < E}. The principal results are: for every bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain Ω and every integer j ≥ 1, |Ω| μ_j(Ω) < 4πj; and, equivalently, N_N(E) > |Ω| E / (4π) for every E > 0. The proof development (about 100,000 lines, namespace PolyaNeumann) also identifies the variational eigenvalues with the spectrum of the constructed self-adjoint Neumann operator, proves a quantitative smooth-domain estimate via boundary transport, Cayley/monodromy rank bounds and a Herglotz-wave reduction, and passes to Lipschitz domains by smooth approximation.
entries.title: Strict Neumann Polya inequality on simply connected planar domains

entries.abstract: For every fixed integer k >= 3, the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of an n-vertex simple graph with at least floor(n^2/4)+1 edges, in which every copy of C_(2k+1) is rainbow, is (1/8 + o(1))n^2. The minimum is attained. The development combines Asad Shahab's seven-cycle proof, using an exact rational five-vertex certificate, with a formalization of the Bucić-Chen-Ma argument for longer odd cycles.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 809: an independent proof of the seven-cycle threshold

entries.abstract: For every real sigma>3/4 and epsilon>0 there exists C>0 such that for all real T>=2, all actual Riemann zeta zeros with Re(rho)>=sigma and |Im(rho)|<=T, counted with analytic multiplicity, number at most C*T^(3*(1-sigma)/(2*sigma)+epsilon). The proof combines separately proved Type I Dirichlet-polynomial large-values and critical-line twelfth-moment bounds. The companion moment is the literal integral on [0,3T] bounded by K*T^(2+epsilon), eventually in T. No analytic premise remains in the final endpoints. Compared with Tao–Trudgian–Yang Table 2 and Kerr Theorem 6, the leading exponent improves for 3/4<sigma<23/29, agrees with the best located leading exponent on [23/29,7/8], and is weaker on (7/8,1). See docs/LITERATURE.md for scope and citations.
entries.title: A zero-density estimate with exponent 3(1−σ)/(2σ) for the Riemann zeta function

entries.abstract: For every fixed complex dimension d at least two, this formalization constructs the specified orthonormal bases of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials in every degree N at least zero. On the complex unit sphere in C^d with surface measure normalized to mass one, the family has Kronecker-delta Gram integrals and spans the full degree-N monomial space. A positive constant depending only on d bounds every basis function on the closed complex Euclidean unit ball, uniformly in N. The explicit formula uses finite Fourier minors, increasing stars-and-bars indices, a square-root-of-two quadratic phase, and the normalization sqrt((N+d-1)!/((d-1)! product alpha_i!)). The proof includes anisotropic cancellation for the actual coupled quadratic form, full zero-extended Poisson finite differences, multinomial conditioning, and Gaussian evaluation of sphere moments. Here explicit refers to the basis formula, not an optimized numerical value of C_d.
entries.title: Explicit uniformly bounded bases of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials in every dimension

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality for bounded, open, simply connected planar domains, including the indexed eigenvalue and counting formulations.
entries.title: Strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality on simply connected planar domains

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the main results of the paper "The generalized Fermat equation x² + y⁵ = z⁷" by Manvir Jaswal. Following Putz, a solution is a triple of integers (X, Y, Z) with X⁵ + Y² = Z⁷, gcd(X, Y, Z) = 1 and XYZ ≠ 0; put η = X⁵/Z⁷ and A_η = ℚ[t]/(f_η), where f_η(t) = 4t⁵ψ(t) − η(4t − 1) and ψ(t) = 25t³ + 20t² + 14t + 14. Theorem 1.1 says that A_η is never isomorphic to Putz's octic field L₈ = ℚ[x]/(h), where h(x) = x⁸ + 4x⁷ − 28x⁶ − 168x⁵ − 140x⁴ + 560x³ + 840x² − 480x − 940. Theorem 1.2 combines this with Putz's Theorem 4.33, which says that A_η is always isomorphic to L₈, to show that x² + y⁵ = z⁷, and equivalently x² + y⁷ = z⁵ and x⁵ + y⁷ = z², have no solution in nonzero coprime integers. The Lean theorems take two hypotheses: Putz's Theorem 4.33 (for Theorem 1.2 only), and that the class group of the ring of integers of L₂₄ = L₈[t]/(ψ) has no element of order 5, which follows from the paper's proof that L₂₄ has class number 1, a computation that is not formalized. The proof follows the paper: a fifth-power descent over L₂₄, completed by fifth-power residue symbols at the primes 101, 131, 181, 251 and 311, with every computation checked by the Lean kernel.
entries.title: The generalized Fermat equation x² + y⁵ = z⁷

entries.abstract: We prove a general interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets and apply it to obtain an improved unconditional lower bound in Sarkozy's theorem, with exponent 0.7580758318008816. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} containing no two distinct elements whose difference is a square, then for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large N we prove D(N) >= N^(0.7580758318008816 - epsilon). The exact exponent is 473797394875551/625000000000000. The reusable criterion starts from finite digit sets in pairwise coprime square bases, with ordered intervals and width-moment inequalities. A strict surplus in the component exponents yields the asymptotic bound through finite stopping words, rank rounding, the Chinese remainder theorem, and interpolation between geometric scales. Both the general criterion and its numerical application are formalized in Lean. All nine concrete components are proved: six prime chains, a 25-state binary recursion, and two complete composite witnesses, at the primes 5 and 43 (three restricted digits at each) and at 19 and 23 (three at 19, two at 23). Every required ordering, numerical moment, lifting, and asymptotic argument is checked, with no remaining finite-certificate hypotheses. This version replaces the exponent 0.75806746 of version 1 with new finite witnesses and more precise certificates. The repository includes self-contained PDF and LaTeX write-ups of the full result and a simpler companion construction attaining exponent 0.758001 that explains several core ideas, together with exact computational certificate programs. The simpler construction is not separately formalized or a selected submission statement.
entries.title: An interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets

entries.abstract: Lean development of the sharp Poincaré inequality for the complex Ginibre log-gas, its two sum-of-squares deficit identities, equality cases, Gaussian Hermite analysis, and the accompanying analytic and stochastic results.
entries.title: Ginibre Poincaré formalization

entries.abstract: A formalization of sharp balanced-law robustness and stability refinements of the classical four-row permanent inequalities of Carlen-Lieb-Loss and Bristiel-Caputo. It proves the exact total-variation radius 1/24, optimal variance-deficit coefficient (1-24r)/9, complete nonnegative equality cases, sharp endpoint entropy constants, and adaptive tensorization. The explicit interior exponent is sufficient rather than optimal; at radius zero it is weaker than the classical optimal uniform exponent. Lean checks exhaustive support coverage and exact rational Gram identities.
entries.title: Sharp robustness and stability of the four-row permanent inequality

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the stability of non-relativistic Coulomb matter in three dimensions. For normalized antisymmetric L2 electron states with q >= 1 spin states and static nuclei with charges between zero and Z, it proves a lower energy bound -C(q,Z)(N+M), uniformly in particle counts and nuclear positions. The main estimate is an additive inequality between nonnegative extended energies, valid even for infinite kinetic energy and nuclear collisions. A real quadratic-form theorem proves Coulomb finiteness and the lower bound for states with finite kinetic energy and distinct nuclear positions. The library also proves the kinetic Lieb-Thirring inequality with Rumin's explicit coefficient (9/35)(6 pi^2)^(2/3) q^(-2/3), Baxter's electrostatic inequality with its positive nearest-other-nucleus correction, and equality of the Fourier kinetic form with the classical Dirichlet integral on spin-valued Schwartz functions. The kinetic normalization is -Delta. The proof combines Pauli projections and Rumin's layer cake, a Voronoi boundary-measure proof of Baxter's inequality, nearest-nucleus screening, and Hardy's inequality. Three extensions prove the atomic bound N < 2Z+1 for weak ground states and strict binding, the unique continuous convex canonical zero-temperature energy density of neutral matter with finite-mass bosonic nuclei in Dirichlet balls, and the molecular Thomas-Fermi large-charge limit for arbitrary fixed spin and every fixed TF mass nu>0. Thomas-Fermi theory also has a unique relaxed minimizer, mass saturation at the total nuclear charge, and exact-mass attainment precisely up to neutrality.
entries.title: Stability of Matter in Lean: Lieb–Thirring, Ionization, the Thermodynamic Limit and Thomas–Fermi Theory

entries.abstract: This development extends OpenAI's Lean proof of the matrix multiplication exponent bound 9/4 from the complex numbers to every field, including finite fields and fields of positive characteristic. It generalizes Fourier separation and interpolation over each field's algebraic closure, descends tensor powers through one fixed finite coefficient algebra, and connects the resulting exact-rank bounds to the original division-free arithmetic-program model. The compared statements include the arithmetic exponent upper bound, nonvacuity and lower-bound checks, an explicit positive-epsilon operation-count theorem, and exact coordinatewise coefficient decompositions. The original numerical bound and complex-field construction are OpenAI's work; this fork contributes the arbitrary-field extension and its formal verification.
entries.title: Matrix multiplication exponent at most 9/4 over arbitrary fields

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Bezdek's annulus theorem and the quantitative area stability of planar plank covers based on the paper "Area stability of plank covers" by Egor Bakaev and Amir Yehudayoff (arXiv:2609.30409). The formalization proves that there exists an explicit positive radius r > 0 such that if finitely many planar planks cover the closed annulus r <= ||x|| <= 1, their total width is at least 2. The core theorem established is the quantitative overlap theorem, which bounds the excess overlap cost on the unit disk from below by a positive constant times the hole area divided by r.
entries.title: Area stability of planar plank covers and Bezdek's annulus theorem

entries.abstract:
The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|.

This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which the cap need not satisfy Baek's injectivity condition, Q(K, B, D) <= |G|, and the cap K lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance 2 sec(phi) sqrt(|G| - Q(K, B, D)) of the horizontal translate of Gerver's cap with the same leftmost point, where phi = 0.039... is Gerver's angle. The proof writes |G| - Q as a sum of nonnegative terms, and the energy terms among them also bound that distance. The bound is attained: Gerver's triple lies in the enlarged domain, and Q equals |G| there.

From the certificate: optimality, Baek's theorem, proved without his Theorem 1.1.1 and without the balance argument of his Chapters 4 to 6; uniqueness, every moving sofa with the area of G is mapped onto G by a rotation and a translation (a translation suffices); and stability, after a translation a moving sofa of area |G| - epsilon lies within Euclidean Hausdorff distance C sqrt(epsilon) of G, their symmetric difference has area at most C' sqrt(epsilon), its rotation angle misses a right angle by at most C'' epsilon, and the exponent 1/2 cannot be improved. The Challenge also states the correspondence between Baek's definitions and those of Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures, and formal-conjectures' statements, among them the uniqueness, which it lists as open; here they are proved through the certificate.

Versions 1 to 4 of this entry registered the formalization of Baek's paper with a first proof of uniqueness that uses his Theorem 1.1.1; they state the same optimality, uniqueness and formal-conjectures theorems, proved through Baek's argument, and the repository keeps their Challenge and Solution in baek/. This version proves those theorems through the certificate and adds the certificate and the stability. A script in the repository, scripts/AuditCoerciveRoute.lean, run by the continuous integration, checks that its proofs reach neither Baek's Theorem 1.1.1, nor the results of his balance argument, nor the main theorem and the equality analysis of the first proof of uniqueness.
entries.title: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 formalization of improved running-time exponents for 3SUM, Exact Triangle, the (min,+)-product and all-pairs shortest paths (APSP), on the word RAM of the published formalization (anthropics/formal-math, 3sum-apsp) of the paper of Alman and Vassilevska Williams, "Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs" (arXiv:2610.06783). That paper gives deterministic algorithms for 3SUM in time O(n^1.9992) and for the (min,+)-product and APSP in time O(n^2.99942), through Exact Triangle in time O(n^(3 - 0.0017)). The project analyzes the same algorithm again and changes it in a few places: an exact count of the leaves of its recursion, a host that charges the solver at the true size of the middle part, and encodings restricted to the leaves that are read. The theorems submitted state, in exactly the sense of upstream's trusted file EndStatement.lean (programs of a word RAM with O(log n)-bit words, numbers of polynomial absolute value, every instance, every size), that 3SUM is solved in O(n^1.99896) steps and Exact Triangle in O(n^2.99791) steps, and, by carrying out the all-edges route that footnote 10 of the paper mentions, that the (min,+)-product and APSP are solved in O(n^2.99791) steps instead of O(n^2.99931) through the standard reductions. None of them has a hypothesis; every proof depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The library also proves general theorems for all admissible parameters, a closed form for the optimal saving of the method at each ratio of parameters, and that the supremum of that saving over all ratios lies in (0.002095, 0.002096], so that no choice of parameters gives 3SUM an exponent below 1.998952 with this method. The pruned encoder and the two new hosts are written as programs of the machine and their running times are proved on it. All Lean, Python and LaTeX was written by the language model Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) in Claude Code, under the direction of the maintainer, who wrote no Lean by hand; the move to Lean v4.35.0-rc2, with the port of the included part of upstream, was made by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) in the same way. An accompanying paper (papers/improved-exponents/) states every result with its Lean name.
entries.title: Improved exponents for 3SUM and APSP from triangles in sparse lopsided graphs

entries.abstract: There exists a locally finite carrier Λ in the real line whose whole complex strongly tempered Meyer space has Hamel dimension ℵ₀. Both a tempered distribution and its distributional Fourier transform have local atomic formulas on Λ, with coefficient families whose absolute values are summable after division by some polynomial weight (1 + |x|)^N. The same carrier supports the entire space; finite-dimensional exponent layers prove the rank upper bound and independent original parity modes prove the lower bound. The radius schedule is selected classically. This is an existence theorem for one carrier, not an effective construction or a classification of all carriers.
entries.title: A strongly tempered Meyer space of countably infinite Hamel dimension

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, checked against Mathlib, of a sharp quantitative propagation of chaos estimate for mean field diffusions dX_i = (a(X_i) + N^{-1} sum_j K(X_i, X_j)) dt + sqrt 2 dW_i with a globally Lipschitz one-body drift a and a bounded, globally Lipschitz pairwise interaction K. If every k-particle marginal of the (possibly correlated and singular) exchangeable initial law lies within squared quadratic Wasserstein distance C_0 (k/N)^2 of the corresponding power of the McKean-Vlasov initial law, then the same holds on every finite time interval [0, T] with an explicit constant C_T that depends neither on N nor on the dimension. No entropy bound, transport inequality or independence of the initial particles is assumed.
entries.title: Sharp Wasserstein propagation of chaos from correlated initial data

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 development around the tensor criterion of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math, family 172). With the criterion's definitions restated character for character from that project's challenge file: every set of six distinct points on a circle satisfies the criterion, by an explicit certificate (the product of the two bilinear forms through the first three and the last three points of a homogeneous parametrisation of the circle, scaled and conjugated by the parametrisation); the sharp dimension theorem: every spherical set of at most m + 4 distinct points, m the dimension of its affine span, satisfies the criterion in its own space and coordinate field (either the augmented vectors admit real isolating quadrics and the sphere lifts by the adjugate, or a dependence among them is supported on six concyclic points while every other point adds a dimension, and the six-point certificate is carried into the ambient space, symmetrised, adjusted to the common sphere, extended point by point and descended from R tensor R to F tensor F), so every spherical set of at most six points satisfies it in any dimension with any affine span; every spherical set with algebraic coordinates satisfies it, of any size, by the separability idempotent of F tensor F; the criterion always implies sphericity, so for algebraic coordinates it is exactly sphericity. Given the sufficiency half of the classification as an explicit hypothesis (quantified as the source states its Theorem 1.1), every spherical set of at most six points, every spherical set of at most m + 4 points and every spanning spherical set with algebraic coordinates is Ramsey; given both halves, a spanning set with algebraic coordinates is Ramsey if and only if it is spherical. The source proves the Ramsey property for at most five circle points; six is the first case its method of independent quadratic rows cannot reach. With the seven-point non-Ramsey circle set of A cyclic non-Ramsey heptagon (arXiv:2609.23327), the least size of a non-Ramsey spherical set is seven, given the classification, and, for m at least 2, m + 5 the least size of one with affine span of dimension m, since the heptagon with m - 2 further sphere points fails the criterion and is not Ramsey; the research note in note/ states this, verifies by an exact derivation identity that the heptagon fails the criterion, and proves the sharpness on paper (nothing in Lean says that a set fails the criterion). The classification is not proved here. The restated definitions and a few adapted lemmas derive from Apache-2.0 work of OpenAI (NOTICE, LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt); the rest is MIT.
entries.title: Six concyclic points satisfy the Euclidean Ramsey tensor criterion, as does every spherical set of at most m + 4 points of affine dimension m and every algebraic spherical set; given the classification's sufficiency half, these sets are Ramsey (the algebraic ones when spanning)

entries.abstract: Formalization of classical factorial-square constructions, exclusion of prime endpoints, existence of minimum representation cardinalities for composite endpoints, and the cutoff D_k = empty for k greater than six. The density question from Erdős problem 374 is defined but not proved. No mathematical novelty or solution of the density problem is claimed.
entries.title: Erdős 374: classical square products of factorials

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Nζ(σ,T) ≪σ,ε T^(2(1−σ)+ε), hence A(σ) ≤ 2, for fixed 3/4 < σ < 1 and ε > 0; zeros with Re(ρ) ≥ σ and 0 < Im(ρ) ≤ T are counted with multiplicity.
entries.title: The density hypothesis for σ > 3/4

entries.abstract: Properly nested nonempty compact connected subsets A and B of a compact metric space are the endpoints of a continuous embedded interval of nonempty compact connected subsets, strictly increasing under inclusion. The ambient space need not be connected.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Order Arcs Between Subcontinua

entries.abstract: The matrix multiplication exponent ω is the least exponent such that n×n matrices can be multiplied in n^(ω+o(1)) operations. This repository proves in Lean 4 / Mathlib that ω < 2.3710449 over every commutative ring, improving the previous bound ω < 2.371177 (Dupont et al. 2026). ω is defined via the exact tensor rank of n×n matrix multiplication. The new ingredient is shared extraction across recursion levels of the asymmetric laser method. The formalization covers the full argument, from the Coppersmith–Winograd degeneration to an exact rational certificate checked in the Lean kernel. The construction and proof were produced largely by AI systems under the authors' direction.
entries.title: LeanMMBound: the matrix multiplication exponent is below 2.3710449

entries.abstract: We give an explicit compact tile, called CLARK (Chair with Local Asymmetric Registration Keys), in five-dimensional Euclidean space. It modifies a chair of 31 unit five-cubes with 256 rational pyramidal keys. Copies may be translated, rotated or reflected. The selected theorem proves tiling existence, no nonzero translation period in any physical tiling, and a finite full Euclidean symmetry group of cardinality at most 3840 for every such tiling. No registration, matching-rule or hierarchy assumption is imposed. A trivial symmetry group is not asserted.
entries.title: The CLARK Tile: An Aperiodic Monotile in Five Dimensions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the theorem that the first Betti number (minimal number of generators of the toric ideal) of a numerical semigroup minimally generated by four elements n0 < n1 < n2 < n3 is at most 2W, where W = (n3 - n0) / gcd(n1 - n0, n2 - n0, n3 - n0); in particular at most twice the width n3 - n0.  This replaces the conjectured quadratic bound (w+1 choose 2) of Herzog–Stamate (2014) and Caviglia–Moscariello–Sammartano (2024) in embedding dimension four; the bound 2w is attained for every width w >= 4 (an informal companion result; sharpness is not formalized).
entries.title: Linear upper bounds for the first Betti number of four-generated numerical semigroups

entries.abstract: We formalize four explicit Szemerédi–Trotter incidence bounds for m distinct points and n distinct affine lines in a field plane. In characteristic zero the bound is 3(mn)^(2/3) + m + n. In positive characteristic p, an arbitrary field admits the additional term 2mn/p. This term is absent when mn ≤ p³. Over the prime field ZMod p the additional term improves to mn/p without a size restriction. The development adapts the author's polynomial-method argument, uses generic coordinates for the improved linear term, and proves a finite-plane counting estimate for the prime-field refinement.
entries.title: Explicit Szemerédi–Trotter bounds over arbitrary fields

entries.abstract: Todorov–Valov Theorem 3.3: for two disjoint closed sets with nonempty interiors in a metric indecomposable continuum, one open cover obstructs every separator map onto every nonempty compact connected Hausdorff target. The classical composant properties remain as foundations.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Alexandroff Property of Metric Indecomposable Continua

entries.abstract: A candidate Lean formalization of fifteen selected statements from Yongxi Lin's table of weak type (1,1) upper bounds for singular integrals and maximal operators. Bounds include full-vector complex-input Riesz, complex Beurling, full and traceless Frobenius Hessians, both projections, centred intervals and balls, and all six Poisson and heat maximal bounds. The strict planar square bound below 3.616 is excluded from the submitted scope at the human author's request.
entries.title: Two partial balayage principles for weak-type estimates

entries.abstract: There is a counterexample to Vaught's conjecture for L_{omega_1,omega}. This formalization is based on an unpublished draft by Robin Knight. It constructs a sentence in a countable relational language with exactly aleph-one isomorphism classes of countable models and no nonempty perfect set of pairwise nonisomorphic model codes. This is not a counterexample to the first-order Vaught conjecture.
entries.title: A counterexample to Vaught's conjecture for infinitary logic

entries.abstract: Block-diagonal matrix factors interleaved with fixed coordinate permutations define low-parametric matrix families. This formalization proves orthogonal-factor sufficiency for two and three real layers, its complex unitary analogue, and explicit four-layer counterexamples over both fields. It establishes an exact two-factor cell-rank criterion and real and unitary cosine-sine exhaustion for the (p,2,p) shuffle family. Two-layer images with complete within-layer block sharing, arbitrary overlap and arbitrary fixed carriers have a smooth atlas in the inherited matrix topology, an exact tangent image, a smooth Frobenius projector, a whole-tangent-bundle Cayley retraction and smooth intrinsic gradient sections. Shared orthogonal block exponential curves have normal ambient acceleration and constant Frobenius speed under the no-off-diagonal-overlap condition. Three-layer (2,q,2) families have genuine topological singularities for every real q >= 3 and for odd unitary q >= 3. The full supported proof library is included; experimental special-unitary drafts and the explicitly listed remaining problems are not claimed.
entries.title: Structured orthogonal and unitary matrices: factorization, geometry and singularities

entries.abstract: Every continuous surjection between compact Hausdorff spaces factors through a compact Hausdorff quotient that collapses exactly the connected components of each original fiber. The first map has connected fibers and the second has totally disconnected fibers. Any two such factorizations have a unique commuting homeomorphism. Empty spaces are permitted.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Monotone-Light Factorization of Compact Hausdorff Surjections

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Catalan's conjecture, proved by Preda Mihăilescu: 8 and 9 are the only consecutive positive proper perfect powers. The formal proof follows the cyclotomic proof in Yuri Bilu's expositions. Cassels' relations, Stickelberger annihilation, and height and counting estimates exclude the case in which one exponent is congruent to 1 modulo the other. Thaine's theorem on circular units, together with a Runge-type approximation argument, settles the remaining case. The class-field-theoretic input comes from a fixed, vendored subset of the ClassFieldTheory library. The registered results are four theorems: Catalan's conjecture over the natural numbers, in the form stated in Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures; the same equation for integer bases greater than one; the classification of solutions of x^p − y^q = 1 with nonzero integer bases of either sign; and Mihăilescu's theorem that x^p = y^q + 1 has no solution in nonzero integers when p and q are odd primes. All four depend only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: A Lean 4 formalization of Catalan's conjecture (Mihăilescu's theorem)

entries.abstract: For a Borel subset E of the Euclidean plane with Hausdorff dimension d in (1, 5/4], a strict upper bound on its packing dimension by the explicit piecewise curve B_H(d) ensures a point y in E whose pinned distance set has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. The three branches are 2d-1, 1+r_2(d-1), and 1/(3-2d), with the transitions and algebraic root defined independently in Challenge.lean. This is a sufficient criterion with an additional packing-dimension hypothesis, not a resolution of the general planar Falconer conjecture.
entries.title: A Hausdorff–packing criterion for self-pinned distance sets

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "The Schur degree of block sums: L(4) = 16 and L(5) ≥ 49" (paper/schur-degree-block-sums.md in this repository). Eliahou and Revuelta (Discrete Math. 344 (2021) 112332) defined a number L(n) through the Schur degree of the set of block sums of a sequence of positive integers, proved S(n−1) + 1 ≤ L(n) ≤ R_{n−1}(3) − 1 and S(n) ≤ n·L(n), and conjectured L(n) = S(n−1) + 1 (their Conjecture 5.6), that is, L(4) = 14 and L(5) = 45. The formalization proves L(4) = 16 (erL_four), 49 ≤ L(5) ≤ 65 (erL_five_bounds), the lift that turns a cover of the nonzero elements of ZMod m₁ × ZMod m₂ by q sets that are sumfree in the group into a sequence whose block sums have Schur degree at most q (lift_lemma), its corollary m₁m₂ ≤ L(n) (le_erL_of_groupPartition), and Theorem 4.1 and the upper bound of Proposition 5.3 of Eliahou and Revuelta, with the pigeonhole bound ramseyBound k in place of R_k(3) (le_sdeg_blockSums, erL_le). So Conjecture 5.6 is false for n = 4 and n = 5. The Lean upper bound for L(5) is 65, not the bound 61 of the paper: the formalization uses the pigeonhole bound R₄(3) ≤ 66 and not the bound R₄(3) ≤ 62 of Fettes, Kramer and Radziszowski. The finite checks use the Lean kernel (decide), with no native code. The sequence W, the lift, the proofs, the programs and the Lean formalization were produced with the AI system Claude (Anthropic; model Claude Opus 5.5) under the direction of the author.
entries.title: The Schur degree of block sums: L(4) = 16 and L(5) ≥ 49

entries.abstract: Hausdorff nullity for all finite products of squared successive logarithms and an upper parabolic box dimension bound of 25/23 for interior singular sets of unforced three-dimensional suitable weak Navier–Stokes solutions.
entries.title: FluidSingularSets

entries.abstract: Every nontrivial compact connected subset of a Hausdorff space contains two distinct points whose individual removals leave connected sets. A compact connected subset containing all non-cut points of a compact connected set equals that set.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Non-Cut Points of Hausdorff Continua

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 disproof of Erdős problem 575 in both its unrestricted and cycle-containing formulations: a finite family F of forbidden graphs containing a bipartite member need not contain a bipartite H ∈ F with ex(n; H) = O(ex(n; F)). Proves the unrestricted case from scratch via the bipartite forest family F_0 = {K_{1,2}, 2K_2} (where ex(n; F_0) ≤ 1 while ex(n; K_{1,2}) ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ and ex(n; 2K_2) ≥ n - 1), and resolves the cycle-containing case by adapting OpenAI's all-bipartite cyclic counterexample family from Erdős problem 180 (where ex(n; F) = O(n^(21/16)) and ex(n; H) = Ω(n^(4/3)) for every H ∈ F).
entries.title: Erdős 575: bipartite extremal-graph compactness

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of an upper bound for the Schur numbers in terms of the triangle Ramsey numbers, and of the structure of a colouring at the limit of that bound. If every colouring with k colours of the pairs of r points has a monochromatic triangle (R_k(3) ≤ r), then the interval [1, 2((k + 1)⌊(r − 1)/2⌋ + 1)] is not covered by k + 1 sumfree sets, so S(k + 1) ≤ 2(k + 1)⌊(r − 1)/2⌋ + 1. With R_2(3) ≤ 6 this gives S(3) ≤ 13, which is exact. Under the hypothesis R_4(3) ≤ 61, a computer-assisted claim of M. Tatarevic that this project does not prove, the pigeonhole step gives R_5(3) ≤ 302, and the bound then gives S(6) ≤ 1801; the hypothesis is an explicit argument (TriangleRamsey 4 61) of each theorem that uses it. The frontier theorems describe a Schur colouring of the largest interval that the bound allows. Let R_k(3) ≤ u + 1, (k + 1)u = 2t and m = (k + 2)t, and let c be a Schur colouring of [1, 2m + 1] with k + 2 colours. Then each colour occurs exactly t times in [1, m]; with q = c(m + 1), the neighbourhood of the centre m in the colour q is regular in every other colour; and c(m + 1 − d) = c(m + 1 + d) for every d in [1, m] with c(d) = q. For six colours under R_4(3) ≤ 61, a Schur colouring of [1, 1801] gives five sets of 60 points, each closed under x ↦ 1800 − x with no fixed point and with differences in at most four colours. These theorems do not exclude such a colouring and do not prove S(6) ≤ 1800. The arguments for the bound and for the frontier were first proposed by AI agents based on ChatGPT (OpenAI) in a project discussion. A Claude agent (Anthropic) audited the argument for the bound; the AI system Claude checked each step of the frontier argument, restated it with explicit hypotheses, and wrote all Lean proofs, under the direction of the author. The results have not been peer reviewed.
entries.title: S(6) ≤ 1801 if R₄(3) ≤ 61: a centred Schur bound and the structure at the frontier

entries.abstract: A nonempty compact connected Hausdorff space covered by countably many pairwise disjoint closed sets has one piece equal to the whole space. Includes arbitrary countable index types, empty pieces, finite partitions, and the continuous-choice corollary.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of unconditional bounds and conditional reductions for Erdős problem 1139 on consecutive P_2 almost-primes (Ω(u_k) ≤ 2). Extending Chojecki's (2026) Erdős 689 double-covering construction via protected-reserve omission, it proves unconditionally that limsup (u_{k+1} - u_k) / log(k + 1) ≥ A > 1 and that every large height X contains an almost-prime-free interval of length ≥ c log X (c > 1), alongside the mixed prime/prime-square CRT bridge, PNT primorial asymptotics, and squared-core deficiency classification. Using a squared-prime core and scale-adaptive dyadic prime shells, it also derives the full infinite-limsup conjecture conditionally from the Green–Tao–Ziegler (2010–2012) linear-forms asymptotic and proves its reverse implication to arbitrary-length prime progressions.
entries.title: Erdős 1139: large gaps between almost-primes

entries.abstract: Over any characteristic-zero field, two elements P and Q of the first Weyl algebra satisfying QP-PQ=1 generate the algebra when P has at most six nonzero homogeneous components for deg X=1 and deg Y=-1. The degree, order and mass of Q are unrestricted. The proof combines sparse-polynomial rigidity with internally proved Newton and Weyl-algebra structural results.
entries.title: The rank-one Dixmier conjecture for elements of mass at most six

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the superdiffusive central limit theorem for a Brownian particle in a critically-correlated incompressible random drift (Armstrong, Bou-Rabee and Kuusi): the quenched superdiffusive invariance principle (Theorem A), quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem (Theorem B), the large-scale C^{0,gamma} and C^{1,gamma} regularity theory (Theorems C and D) and the sharp asymptotics of the renormalized diffusivities (Theorem 5.1), with every result of Sections 2 to 8 of the paper that their proofs use. It is built on the public CoarseGraining homogenization library and the public MarkovProcess library.
entries.title: Superdiffusive central limit theorem for a Brownian particle in a critically-correlated incompressible random drift

entries.abstract:
A conditional Lean 4 formalization of E. Markman, "Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds" (arXiv:2502.03415v2). The paper proves that the Hodge-Weil classes of polarized abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 are algebraic (Theorem 1.5.1) and deduces the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Corollary 1.6.1).

Every result of the paper about cohomology classes, Clifford algebras, spin representations, Hodge structures and period domains is proved in a linear-algebra model of the cohomology of abelian varieties (abelian varieties up to isogeny as polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight one), by the paper's arguments except the departures listed under fidelity (notably Proposition 6.1.2 and Lemma 4.0.2, proved by other arguments with the owner's approval): rational secant lines to the spinor variety and the abelian 2n-folds of Weil type they give (Sections 2-4), the Spin(V)-equivariance of Orlov's equivalence (Section 6, Proposition 6.1.2), Theorem 1.4.1(3) and (4) (the characteristic class of the secant-square sheaf stays of Hodge type on every Weil-type deformation of X x X^, and its K-translates with h^3 span Q h^3 + HW), Corollary 1.3.2, the cohomological results of Section 8, and Section 10. The results the paper cites from Chevalley, Igusa (Lemmas 1-2, Section 2, Proposition 3 except the orbits over subfields in which -d is not a square), Golyshev-Lunts-Orlov, Orlov, Huybrechts, Trautman, van Geemen (Def. 4.9, and Th. 5.2(3) through Landherr's theorem and Meyer's theorem), Markman (2023) and Schoen (Prop. 10, from push-forward of cycles, by Voisin's argument) are proved in the case the paper uses.

Theorem 1.5.1 and Corollary 1.6.1 are proved assuming, as named hypotheses in their statements, the paper's own sheaf-theoretic Sections 7-9 (in the form: the class kappa_3(E) is algebraic near X x X^ wherever kappa(E) is of Hodge type) and results from algebraic geometry not yet available in Lean: about algebraic cycles, pullbacks, push-forwards along projections and products of algebraic classes, the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, Voisin's algebraicity loci and a theorem of Ramon-Mari; about Hodge structures, two theorems of Moonen-Zarhin. Remark 10.1.2(1) assumes part of Igusa's Proposition 3 when -d is not a square. Eleven statements of the paper are false or misprinted as printed and are formalized in corrected form (the basis of Example 10.2.2 is also misprinted, with no effect on the value computed there); REPORT.md audits the paper.
entries.title: Weil classes on abelian sixfolds and the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds (Markman)

entries.abstract: A formalization and provably correct implementation of a linear-time algorithm for triangulating a simple polygon.  The implementation is a concrete program for an explicit exact real RAM.  Lean proves that on every simple polygon with n vertices the program halts within C(n+1) steps, with natural-number words at most K(n+1), and outputs a conforming triangulation with exactly n - 2 triangles on the input vertices.  No general-position assumption is made.  The proofs use exactly Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), with no sorry and no native_decide.  They are checked by the Lean kernel and replayed by independent kernels.  The algorithm is a variant of Chazelle's (B. Chazelle, Triangulating a simple polygon in linear time, Discrete & Computational Geometry 6 (1991), 485-524), and the main theorem is the triangulation conclusion of his Theorem 4.3.  The program follows the structure of Chazelle's algorithm: visibility maps of polygonal chains, merging with conformality restoration and granularity enforcement, ray-shooting and arc-cutting oracles built with planar separators, the up phase and the down phase, and the final stage from the visibility map to the triangulation.  It departs from the paper's algorithm in documented ways; in particular its down phase recurses only for n >= 2^30 + 2.  The running-time bound is proved for this program, not for the algorithm as the paper describes it.  The program is also given by name with explicit (very large) constants, and a merge-level refinement theorem shows that its run follows an abstract model of the algorithm written from the paper.
entries.title: Linear-Time Triangulation of Simple Polygons (Chazelle's Algorithm) in Lean 4

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of all three parts of Erdős problem 1054. For the least integer f(n) whose k smallest divisors sum to n, we prove that f(n) is not o(n), is not o(n) on any density-one set, and satisfies limsup f(n)/n = ∞ on every density-one subtype. Building on the qualitative divisor-prefix sieve and almost-all binary Goldbach proof from Principia-Math-Solutions, this formalization proves the Formal Conjectures statements along with a sharp second-moment lower-density bound c / [A^3 (1 + log A)^4] for odd n with f(n) > A n, the Tao–Kovač small-ratio upper bound #{n ≤ X : 0 < f(n) ≤ δ n} ≤ C δ^3 X, liminf_{f(n)>0} f(n)/n = 0, and the asymptotic density equivalence between {s(2d)} and even aliquot values.
entries.title: Erdős 1054: sums of smallest divisors

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of the negative answer to Erdős problem 958: for every n ≥ 4, there exists an n-point configuration in the Euclidean plane determining n - 1 distinct interpoint distances with multiplicities {1, 2, ..., n - 1} that is neither equidistant on a line nor equidistant on a circle. Formalizing the May 2025 construction of Clemen, Dumitrescu, and Liu, the proof places n - 1 equally spaced points on a short arc of the unit circle together with the center (0, 0), uses strict monotonicity of chord lengths on [0, π/3) to compute the exact distance-multiplicity profile, and eliminates collinear and concyclic progressions algebraically. It also proves the positive baseline results that every equidistant collinear configuration of size n ≥ 2 has n - 1 distinct distances with multiplicities {1, ..., n - 1}, and that for every n ≥ 2 there exists an n-point circular equidistant configuration with that distance-multiplicity profile.
entries.title: Erdős 958: planar point sets with distance multiplicities {1, ..., n - 1}

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of the negative answer to Erdős problem 2 (Hough 2015; Balister–Bollobás–Morris–Sahasrabudhe–Tiba 2022): there is an absolute constant B such that every finite covering of the integers by distinct moduli > 1 contains a modulus ≤ B. For any finite set D of moduli above B with N = lcm(D), the proof builds a probability measure on ZMod N prime by prime via the BBMST half-cap fiber update, preserving the progression bound w(z ≡ a mod d) ≤ 2^ω(d)/d while bounding each prime-p loss by C (log p)^6 / (p - 1)^2 via Euler factorization and Mertens' third theorem. Combining this summable tail with Euler's product bound on A-smooth reciprocals keeps the covered mass below 1/2, proving the Formal Conjectures ideal statement (erdos_2), its direct negation (not_arbitrarilyLarge_ideal_coverings), the uniform minimum-modulus bound (minimum_modulus_bound), and finite-set noncoverage (finite_noncoverage_bound).
entries.title: Erdős 2: minimum modulus of distinct covering systems

entries.abstract: Higher-cell attachment invariance for ordinary topological fundamental groups. For any path-connected topological space X, any basepoint, an index type in an independent universe, independently varying cell dimensions at least three, and arbitrary continuous unit-sphere attaching maps, the genuine adjunction quotient of X and the coproduct of closed Euclidean unit balls is constructed with its quotient topology. The actual inclusion-induced fundamental-group homomorphism is bijective and is the underlying homomorphism of the displayed multiplicative equivalence. Mixed dimensions and the empty family are included. No finiteness, countability, CW, separation or local-connectivity hypotheses are added, and no retraction, simple-connectivity or kernel oracle is assumed.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Fundamental Groups of Arbitrary Higher-Cell Attachments

entries.abstract: The full arbitrary-family two-cell attachment theorem for ordinary topological fundamental groups. For any path-connected topological space X, any basepoint, and any indexed family of continuous circle attaching maps, a genuine adjunction quotient is constructed from X and the coproduct of closed complex unit disks. The actual inclusion-induced fundamental-group homomorphism is surjective and its kernel is precisely the normal closure of the once-around attaching loops, transported along the specified basepoint paths. A quotient group isomorphism is proved compatible with the actual inclusion map. No finiteness, CW, separation, local-connectivity or semilocal-simple-connectivity hypotheses are added.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Fundamental Groups of Arbitrary Two-Cell Attachments

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of the affirmative answer to Erdős problem 546 (Sudakov's theorem): there exists an absolute constant C > 0 such that every finite simple graph G with m edges and no isolated vertices has diagonal Ramsey number R(G) ≤ 2^(C √m). Formalizing Sudakov's 2011 proof—including high-degree vertex deletion, greedy bounded-degree embedding and hereditary sparse cuts, low-density monochromatic-pair extraction, and iterative clique-reservoir amplification. This proves the uniform explicit bound R(G) ≤ 2^(4000 √m) across all finite simple graphs without isolated vertices (including m = 0), together with the exact Formal Conjectures statement.
entries.title: Erdős 546: sparse graph Ramsey numbers

entries.abstract: A fully-dynamic Maximum-Cardinality-Search (MCS) ordering algorithm that, on a single-edge insertion or deletion into a loop-free undirected graph, scans the affected window between the two endpoints for the first step at which the current ordering's choice stops being a legal MCS pick, and only then regreedies the suffix (probe-then-repair). Correctness - every order produced stays a valid MCS ordering of the updated graph, and in fact equals the from-scratch canonical ordering - is machine-checked in Lean 4 / Mathlib, together with locality (the first position whose choice can change lies inside the window between the endpoints; after a break the suffix is regreedyed, so positions past the window may also change), an executable boolean-adjacency implementation proved to refine the abstract update, and per-update cost in a unit-cost query model (counting legality checks and pick steps along the real executable control flow): at most n units for an insertion and n + 1 for a deletion, so the worst case matches static recomputation. A stability-boundary result is also proved: if the neighbour count of every vertex in one graph exceeds that in the other by at most one along every chosen prefix, the two graphs admit a common MCS ordering; in particular inserting or deleting a matching, or flipping a single edge, always preserves a common MCS ordering.
entries.title: Dynamic MCS Ordering Maintenance

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of the affirmative answer to Erdős problem 956: for all sufficiently large n, there exist n pairwise-disjoint translates of a compact convex planar set with more than n^(1+c) unordered pairs at Euclidean set-distance 1 (for c = 1/4). Adapting the parabolic construction announced by Valtr (2005) and detailed in Chojecki's April 2026 manuscript, the formalization proves the supporting-hyperplane theorem for a centrally symmetric signed parabolic cap and constructs a four-layer parabolic grid of disjoint translates. This establishes the explicit lower bound h(n) > (1/26) n^(4/3) for all n ≥ 80 and the sharper eventual bound h(n) > (2/5) n^(4/3).
entries.title: Erdős 956: unit distances between disjoint convex translates

entries.abstract: The critical-window laws for autocatalytic emergence in reversible binary-polymer networks lead to survival profiles for independent open reaction channels. For both the ordered split-position and commuting-factor quotient models, with all binary words of length at most two as food, explicit total algorithms enclose each survival probability at every rational openness in [0,1] to any prescribed positive rational accuracy. Computable seed lengths and finite-record contraction estimates provide uniform truncation bounds on intervals bounded away from zero. The associated intensity profiles S(1 − exp(−λ)) are smaller than every fixed power of λ as λ tends to zero from above. Rational interval bounds also compare these profiles with finite-network RAF-existence probabilities under explicit catalyst-pool and input-probability conditions. These results extend the split and quotient critical-window laws with certified approximation and quantitative control.
entries.title: Effective approximation and low-intensity flatness of RAF critical-window profiles

entries.abstract: Every connected finite simple graph admits an edge partition into at most ceil(|V(G)|/2) simple paths when at most two vertices of its induced even-degree graph have degree greater than three. One positive designated even vertex can be exposed twice at the ceiling budget. Two designated even vertices can be exposed twice simultaneously within floor(|V(G)|/2)+1 paths, giving simultaneous ceiling exposure at odd order. Exceptional and ordinary degrees are unrestricted. Simultaneous even-order ceiling exposure and the unrestricted Gallai conjecture are not claimed.
entries.title: Gallai's conjecture with two exceptional even vertices

entries.abstract:
A formalization of E. S. Allman, J. H. Degnan and J. A. Rhodes, "Identifying the rooted species tree from the distribution of unrooted gene trees under the coalescent", J. Math. Biol. 62 (2011) 833-862. The multispecies coalescent is defined from Kingman's coalescent on forests of gene lineages (its generator, the matrix exponential, and a recursion over the species tree).

Proved: the distribution of unrooted topological gene trees, with one lineage sampled per taxon, determines the rooted species tree and its internal branch lengths when there are at least five taxa (Theorem 9); on four taxa it determines exactly the unrooted metric species tree (Proposition 3); with several lineages per taxon it also determines the corresponding pendant branch lengths (Corollary 10); and all of this holds for nonbinary species trees (Proposition 11). Every other result of the paper is proved too, with the explicit gene tree distributions, linear invariants and inequalities for five taxa, and the cited results that the proofs use: Tavare's formula, the reconstruction of trees from quartets, and Cayley's count of tree shapes.
entries.title: Identifying the rooted species tree from unrooted gene trees under the coalescent

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Theorems A and B of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. For every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic order of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex central configuration with that cyclic order, up to similarity, so there are exactly three convex central configurations up to similarity. This answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos (2012). The main step of the paper is Theorem B: at every strictly convex central configuration of positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least one quarter of its radial part K. It follows that every convex central configuration is a nondegenerate local minimum of U I^(1/2), whose Hessian vanishes exactly on the tangent space of the orbit of the similarities. The computer-assisted step, a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations in the coordinates of Corbera, Cors and Roberts, proves tr S < 3/4 and is checked by Lean's kernel with `decide +kernel` in 7307 certificate theorems. No compiled code is trusted, and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.
entries.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the quantum Pauli basis test from MIP*=RE. The comparator-configured results give a value-one symmetric projective consistent commuting strategy, quantum soundness of the simultaneous low-degree test, soundness of the Pauli basis test up to local isometries with the explicit deltaQld error, and the corresponding qubit-coordinate form.
entries.title: Quantum Pauli basis test

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.
entries.title: Stafford 3.8

entries.abstract: A Lean-checked proof of FKS Problem 1 for graphs on at most 2d vertices, for every d ≥ 4: every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most d with no connected component isomorphic to K_{d+1} has an injective placement in Euclidean d-space, with every vertex of norm 1/√2 and every edge at distance exactly 1. Non-edges are unconstrained and may also have length 1. The unrestricted question is false at d = 4: Mishra and Senthilkumar (2026) showed that the square of the nine-cycle, on 2d + 1 = 9 vertices, has no such placement. The bound proved here is therefore sharp at d = 4. Neither result settles the question restricted to d ≥ 5. The exception is interpreted componentwise: a K_{d+1} component already precludes such a placement even when other components are present. The research audience is discrete geometers and extremal graph theorists studying spherical unit-distance representations, graph dimension and bounded-degree embedding problems.
entries.title: FKS Problem 1 on at most twice the dimension vertices

entries.abstract: A Lean proof that every family of 14-element subsets of a 24-element set covering all 4-element subsets has at least 20 members, so the covering number C(24,14,4) is at least 20, improving the previously tabulated lower bound of 19. Point derivation (the Schönheim bound) then gives C(25,15,5) >= 34, improving the tabulated 32. The proof excludes a hypothetical 19-block covering using degree and codegree counting, a Gram-matrix rank argument that forces balanced bipartite components, and a structural analysis of the two resulting cases.
entries.title: Lower bounds for the covering numbers C(24,14,4) and C(25,15,5)

entries.abstract: The full cycle characterization for arbitrary finite player types and arbitrary nonempty player-dependent action spaces. A real-valued exact potential exists if and only if deviators' payoff differences sum to zero around every finite closed path, every finite simple closed path, every simple four-cycle, or every two-player rectangle. The construction uses finite-subset induction and imposes no finiteness restriction on actions. Exact potentials are unique up to an additive constant. With finite actions, the cycle condition yields a pure Nash equilibrium. Adversarial examples distinguish matching pennies, infinite actions, unequal dependent actions, and the finite-action boundary.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Monderer–Shapley Exact-Potential Characterization

entries.abstract: Substantive Lean development for labelled distance-shell observations of anonymous integer populations. The focused 14-statement interface covers six result groups. Square grids have an exact four-corner interval-cut characterization of recovery of all populations of mass at most two after one erased report, an equivalent distance-sum compression contract, and exact corner-constrained optimum ceil(3(n+1)/2) for every n at least 3. For every positive q, the actual-distance equalizer cardinality of Q_(4q) lies between 2^(4q-1)+2q-1 and 2^(4q-1)+2q; explicit prefixes also give the infinite contradiction to the sourced exponential formula. Further selected results prove the long-rectangle optimum, ordinary 2-domination on every positive even bishop board, two exact Petersen double-total-domination values, and a connected real fractional-face counterexample. The complete library is included, not an external or assumption-based wrapper. Supporting algebra and geometric lemmas remain proved but unselected. The public README explains mathematical scope, antecedents, and limitations without treating known ingredients or all supporting lemmas as separate original results.
entries.title: Distance-Shell Tomography: Geometric Certificates for Fault-Tolerant Sensing, Moment Compression, and Hypercube Equalization

entries.abstract: A full constructive formalization of the Falmagne–Block–Marschak theorem for any finite nonempty alternative set, without a cardinality bound. A normalized stochastic choice rule on all nonempty menus is generated by a single probability distribution over complete strict rankings if and only if all Block–Marschak alternating-sum coefficients are nonnegative. The proof derives Boolean-lattice flow conservation, constructs a finite ranking mixture by positive-path subtraction, and proves exact lower-contour probability identities by Möbius inversion. Compiled adversarial examples show that regularity alone is insufficient.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Falmagne–Block–Marschak Random-Utility Characterization

entries.abstract: Milgrom and Shannon (1994), Theorem 4, in both directions: for an arbitrary lattice X, partially ordered parameter space T, and real-valued objective, strong-set monotonicity of constrained maximizers over every pair of strongly ordered feasible subsets is equivalent to quasisupermodularity of every section and both weak and strict preference-preservation clauses of single crossing. The theorem imposes no finiteness, completeness, topology, continuity, compactness, nonemptiness, or optimizer existence assumptions. Supporting results and counterexamples distinguish crossing clauses and fixed-domain from varying-feasible-set monotonicity. Earlier Lean sufficiency results in Econlib and nonmathlib4 are explicitly cited.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Milgrom–Shannon's Monotonicity Theorem: the Full Characterization

entries.abstract: Formalization of all the numbered statements of F. Marbach, "Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems" (2026), https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00022. For abstract linear control systems in the sense of Weiss (a strongly continuous semigroup T on a Banach space X and bounded input maps Phi_t : L^p(R_+; U) -> X satisfying the concatenation identity), the main results are: for p = infinity, every system is zero-class, i.e. the operator norm of Phi_t tends to zero as t -> 0+ (Theorem 1.5), and t -> Phi_t u is continuous on [0, infinity) for every u in L^infinity (Corollary 1.6), a positive answer to Weiss' 1989 Problem 2.4. No integral representation of the input maps is assumed. The proof packs nearly extremal controls into one bounded operator on l^infinity and uses Phillips' lemma (Lemma 2.2), which is proved here. The development also covers the continuity of semigroup orbits (Proposition 1.2), the classical case p < infinity (Proposition 1.3), and the examples of Section 3: a non zero-class system for p < infinity (Proposition 3.1), an exotic invariant mean on periodic L^infinity functions (Lemma 3.2), and a scalar system with p = infinity without integral representation and not E_F-admissible for any Young function F (Proposition 3.3).
entries.title: Continuity of solutions to abstract linear control systems

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of two classical regularity theorems for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations. The Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák theorem states that a Leray–Hopf solution whose spatial L³ norm remains bounded in time is smooth at positive times and unique among Leray–Hopf solutions with the same initial data. The Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin theorem gives the corresponding conclusion under a family of mixed space-time integrability conditions. The development includes the local regularity theorem, L⁵ space-time integrability under the endpoint L³ condition, and the supporting Carleman inequalities, unique continuation and backward uniqueness. It builds on the Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg formalization and includes a manuscript presenting the proofs.
entries.title: Escauriaza–Seregin–Šverák and Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin regularity

entries.abstract: Kamenica and Gentzkow's finite-state persuasion theorem from economic primitives: nonempty compact metric actions, continuous sender and receiver utilities, and a full-support common prior. Receiver best replies and sender-preferred tie actions exist. The induced sender payoff is bounded and upper semicontinuous. Finite signals realize exactly finite Bayes-plausible posterior splittings, with prescribed posteriors recovered only at nonnull messages. An optimal finite signal with at most the number of states plus two messages exists and dominates every finite experiment. Its value is the least concave majorant of the induced payoff on the entire belief simplex; strict persuasion gain is exactly the concavification gap. This covers the signal/splitting part of Proposition 1 and Corollary 2, including attainment. The straightforward recommendation branch and compact-state extension are outside this scope. Related finite splitting and abstract attainment are already formalized in Daniel Lyng's Econlib; no first-formalization or novelty claim is made.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Optimal Information and Concavification in Bayesian Persuasion

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Constantin, Ignatova and Vicol on the regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with analytic forcing (arXiv:2609.20803). A suitable weak solution on the unit parabolic cylinder, smooth before the blow-up time, whose force is bounded in C^2 up to the blow-up time and real analytic in space, whose angular mean satisfies anisotropic Type II bounds, and which is exactly axisymmetric on a ball around the axis at every time, is axisymmetric and regular at the putative singular point (Theorem 1.1); the axisymmetric theorem (Theorem 1.3), the meridional smallness proposition, the consequences for the force (Corollary 2.3) and the lemmas of Sections 3 and 5 are formalized with it. The interior analyticity theorem of Kahane, the interior estimates of Serrin and the regularity criterion of Gustafson, Kang and Tsai, in the forms the paper uses, are proved rather than assumed. The thirteen results use only the standard axioms and build on the Lean formalization of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg theorem; five of them are restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge and proved from the library theorems.
entries.title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric Navier–Stokes solutions with analytic forcing

entries.abstract: A Lean formalisation of a hitting time theorem of Wanfang Chen, Jared León and Xizhi Liu. For every fixed integer r ≥ 3, assume all r-element subsets of n vertices are exposed in a uniformly random order. As n tends to infinity through multiples of r − 1, with probability tending to one, a loose Hamilton cycle first emerges exactly when the last isolated vertex disappears.
entries.title: The hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in r-graphs

entries.abstract: A general two-alternative implementation characterization on own-type domains containing an open ball: affine private and social valuation differences, nonzero social linear form, one active welfare cut, and a fixed independent opposing probability law force nonnegative coefficient alignment. Arbitrary measurable efficient lotteries have integrable Bayesian incentive compatible transfers exactly under alignment, with explicit ex-post truthful-opponent transfers and a measurable efficient allocation witness. Arbitrary distributions including atoms are covered. A genuine independent uniform-square auction model rules out efficiency even under only agent 0 incentive compatibility for every a,b>0. The separately proved finite sharp welfare/error frontier and original example corollary are retained. This does not formalize arbitrary-alternative Theorem 4.3 or genericity, and makes no novelty claim.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of p-adic valuation laws for alternating cofactors C_d(p^a) = (p^(ad)+1)/(p^a+1) with odd d. It proves finite-window coefficient scaling and an exact pre-extremal restricted-binomial-gcd formula, identifies the sparse endpoint, proves the least extremal row T_p(C_d(p^a)) = p^(ad)+1 for odd d >= 5, and gives the full cubic classification for p^(2a)-p^a+1. The Palomar Challenge records coefficient scaling, the exact bounded gcd formula, the odd-degree least-row theorem, and the cubic classification.

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 proof of the Cook–Levin theorem and of the NP-completeness of several variants of satisfiability, for an explicit machine model, using only Lean's core library. The compared theorems state that the following languages are NP-complete: SAT, the set of binary codes of satisfiable CNF formulas (Complexity.sat_np_complete); 3-SAT, with at most three literals per clause (threeSAT_np_complete); exactly-3-SAT, with exactly three literals per clause on three distinct variables (exactThreeSAT_np_complete); (≤1,≤2)-SAT, with two or three literals per clause and every variable occurring at most once positively and at most twice negatively (leOneLeTwoSAT_np_complete); SAT with variable indices written in binary (binarySAT_np_complete); planar 3-SAT, whose variable–clause incidence graph is planar (planarThreeSAT_np_complete); and Lichtenstein's planar 3-SAT, whose incidence graph stays planar with the cycle through the variables added (cyclePlanarThreeSAT_np_complete). Planarity is Gonthier's from the formal proof of the Four Color Theorem: a graph is planar when a hypermap on its half-edges embeds it with genus zero, the genus being computed from the Euler formula. NP-complete means: in NP, and every language in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one (Karp) reduction. A further compared theorem, inNP_iff_nondeterministicPolyTime, proves that NP, defined by verifiers, is the class of languages accepted in polynomial time by nondeterministic machines with two transition tables. Languages are sets of binary words. Computation is by deterministic Turing machines with a single two-way infinite tape over a four-symbol alphabet, and time is the number of machine steps. NP is defined by polynomial-time verifiers and polynomially bounded certificates, the standard certificate characterization; a reduction is a function computed by such a machine within a polynomial number of steps. Formulas are coded with unary variable indices and list lengths (binary indices for the binary variant); words that code no formula belong to none of the languages.
For an arbitrary NP verifier, the hardness proof builds a CNF formula describing the computation tableau of the verifier on the input and an unknown certificate; it is satisfiable exactly when some certificate makes the verifier accept. The reduction is itself implemented as a machine: it is written in a small language of loops over unary counters, compiled through finite programs on Boolean stacks to the single-tape model, and its running time is proved by counting the executed steps. SAT is reduced to 3-SAT by replacing each clause with a chain of clauses of at most three literals linked by fresh variables, and the reductions are composed as machines. Exactly-3-SAT and (≤1,≤2)-SAT are reached by transforming the Cook–Levin formula generator itself: every literal occurrence gets its own copy variable, a cycle of implications links the copies of each variable, long clauses are split by chains, and short clauses are padded. The binary variant is reached by a machine converting unary indices to binary. For planar 3-SAT, the Cook–Levin formula is turned into a grid formula in the style of Lichtenstein (one column of crossover gadgets per clause, copies of each variable joined by nested two-literal clauses), proved equisatisfiable and planar with its variable cycle through a general lemma on formulas drawn as combs; the plain version subdivides the cycle edges. Membership in NP is proved with explicit verifier machines for every language; for the planar versions the certificate also describes a planar embedding. For the nondeterministic characterization, a deterministic verifier simulates a nondeterministic machine with its choices read from the certificate, and conversely a nondeterministic machine guesses a certificate in a unary budget and runs the verifier. The development was written by AI under human direction: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) produced the proof, and Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) ran its full verification, revised the statement for auditability and prepared it for Palomar, with the variants and the nondeterministic characterization proved by Claude agents. The proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

entries.abstract: Hordijk and Steel (https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.03919, Section 7, Eq. (21)) conjectured a zero-one threshold for RAF emergence at linear mean catalysis. An interior limiting law is established for the reversible binary-polymer model with monomer/dimer food and reaction channels obtained by identifying the split descriptions u + v and v + u precisely when uv = vu. Each molecule independently catalyzes each channel, with one catalysis coordinate shared by both directions. For every real sequence f(n)/n → λ > 0, the clamped channel parameter eventually equals f(n)/|J_n|, and the probability of a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set converges to a limit L(λ) depending only on λ. The function L is nondecreasing and satisfies 0 < L(λ) ≤ 1 − exp(−34λ) < 1 at every positive finite intensity. Thus a zero-one step threshold is excluded in this channel model.

entries.abstract: Finite Gershkov–Goeree–Kushnir–Moldovanu–Shi (2013) Theorem 2 for arbitrary finite agents and alternatives, heterogeneous ordered finite scalar type supports, arbitrary independent positive support masses, and linear private values with nonnegative slopes and arbitrary constants. The library constructs a feasible dominant-strategy mechanism preserving every support type's interim expected utility and ex ante social surplus. Weighted monotone lifting is proved by a compact feasible quadratic minimizer and an improving perturbation. Adjacent transfer bounds imply full-report IC by telescoping. Selected results are finite equivalence, weighted monotone lifting and optimizer monotonicity; scalar IC and support-restriction facts remain in the library as supporting lemmas. Validation evidence is recorded separately for the exact candidate.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization" (arXiv:2305.05048). For every alpha in (0, 1/3) it constructs one divergence-free, Z^2-periodic drift b in C^0_t C^{0,alpha}_x intersect C^{0,alpha}_t C^0_x on [0,1] x T^2, and proves three properties of the advection-diffusion equation with this drift: anomalous dissipation of scalar variance for every mean-zero H^1 datum (Theorem 1.1 of the paper); a uniform C^{0,mu}([0,1]; L^2) bound by C times the H^1 norm of the datum along a set of diffusivities accumulating at zero (Remark r.LeBron.2); and non-uniqueness of vanishing-diffusivity limits for a class of data containing cos(2 pi n x_1) for infinitely many n (a corrected form of the paper's no-selection principle). The three properties are combined in one theorem, restated in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge. The formalization also proves existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and the classical facts the paper uses without proof.

entries.abstract: Bergemann–Morris Theorem 1 for arbitrary finite players and states with heterogeneous action and original-signal spaces: a normalized decision rule is obedient if and only if a finite marginal-preserving information expansion supports a valid mixed Bayes–Nash strategy profile inducing its joint law. The recommendation expansion and the converse for arbitrary extra signals and independent behavioral randomization are proved. Null fibers are handled without conditioning, and exact induction is equivalent to the paper's positive-support quotient. Zero prior masses are permitted, extending the paper's full-support assumption. The one-player decision-problem specialization and explicit examples are included. Theorem 2 proves that individual sufficiency is equivalent to BCE outcome inclusion across all finite basic games with arbitrary heterogeneous actions and utilities and full-support common priors, on a nonempty finite state space. Its converse constructs actual couplings from finite quadratic-scoring games and weighted compactness.

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the AGV (d'Aspremont-Gérard-Varet-Arrow) expected-externality mechanism: with independent types, ex post efficiency, Bayesian incentive compatibility, and budget balance are jointly attainable. Agents are indexed by Fin n with 2 ≤ n; each agent has a finite nonempty type space with an independent PMF prior; alternatives form a finite nonempty type; values are private. The efficient rule xmax maximizes utilitarian welfare, and agvTransfer pays each agent its expected externality minus an equal share of the other agents' receipts. Interim individual rationality is not claimed.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Herzog–Schönheim conjecture (the index form, which implies the cardinality form asked in Erdős problem 274) for every solvable group, finite or infinite: if a solvable group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, left cosets of subgroups, then two of the subgroups have the same index (hence, in the cardinality form, the same cardinality). The conjecture for arbitrary groups is open and is not claimed. The infinite case reduces to a finite solvable quotient by the common core of the parts; the finite case is proved for a least counterexample by considering its largest prime divisor p, using the subgroup generated by the p-prime-part elements, divisibility restrictions on local indices obtained from fixed-point counts in a primitive solvable quotient, and an extra closure argument at p = 7. The statements use the same exact covering structure as the formal-conjectures file for Erdős problem 274.
entries.title: The Herzog–Schönheim conjecture for solvable groups

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Cremer-McLean full surplus extraction theorem (Econometrica, 1988): for a single indivisible object with finitely many bidders, finite type spaces, and a correlated joint prior with full support, if every bidder's family of conditional distributions over the others' types is convex independent (no conditional lies in the convex hull of the rest), then there exists a Bayesian incentive compatible, interim individually rational direct mechanism that allocates ex post efficiently and extracts the full surplus: every bidder's interim expected utility is zero, so expected seller revenue equals the expected maximum value. The proof hinges on constructing side-bet lotteries with zero own-conditional expectation and strictly positive cross-conditional expectation, obtained by strict separation of each conditional from the convex hull of the others, scaled to dominate any misreport gain.
