entries.abstract: For n = 1, …, 7: the least radius of a closed disk holding n unit squares with disjoint interiors, each placed and rotated freely, and every packing that attains it. The radii are √2/2, √5/2, 5√17/16, √2, √(5/2), √q* ≈ 1.68854 and √13/2, where q* is a quartic irrational. Up to rotation about the disk centre and relabelling, the optimal packing is unique for n ≤ 6: the square, the 2 × 1 rectangle, the T, the 2 × 2 block, the plus, and for six squares a central square with four neighbours, two of them pushed along its sides, and a sixth square turned by π/4 between those two. For n = 7 the optimal packings form a three-parameter family: two columns of two squares and, between them, a column of three whose heights vary independently, at least 1 apart and within √3 − 1/2 of the disk centre. The proofs for three to six squares bound the arcs the squares occupy on a small circle about the disk centre. For six squares this finds the square that contains the disk centre; five fixed points label the others, and a weighted sum of separating inequalities, with estimates uniform in the angles of the squares, forces the optimal radius. For seven squares, each square avoiding the disk centre gets a direction from it, and in the optimal disk two disjoint such squares get directions at least π/3 apart. We found no earlier proof for five, six or seven squares, and no exact one for three, where a computer-assisted enclosure of the radius and the optimal arrangements was known. Four squares, uniqueness included, were settled by hand in 2026, by the same idea as here.
entries.title: Optimal packings of one to seven unit squares in a disk

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of H. T. Pham and L. Sauermann, "On Graham's rearrangement conjecture" (arXiv:2602.15797v1). Graham conjectured in 1971 that for every prime p, every subset S of Z_p \ {0} has an ordering whose partial sums are pairwise distinct. The formalization proves the paper's main theorem (Theorem 1.2): for every 0 < α < 1 there is a constant C_α > 0 such that, for every prime p, every S ⊆ Z_p \ {0} with C_α ≤ |S| ≤ p^(1-α) has such an ordering. It also proves the paper's anticoncentration bounds for the sum of a uniformly random m-element subset R of a set S ⊆ Z_p with |S| ≥ 2: the probability that the sum of R equals any given z is at most 1/p + C/(|S|√m), for an absolute constant C > 0, when C log|S| ≤ m ≤ 10^-3 |S|/log|S| (Theorem 1.3), and, for every 0 < ε < 1, at most 1/p + C_ε √(log|S|)/(|S|√m) for every positive integer m ≤ (1-ε)|S| (Corollary 1.4). Every result that the paper proves is formalized, following its argument, and so are the two hypergeometric tail bounds that its proofs take from the Chernoff bound of Janson, Łuczak and Ruciński.
entries.title: On Graham's rearrangement conjecture (Pham–Sauermann)

entries.abstract: Two components of the proof, in the paper "Linnik's constant is at most 3.99" (paper/linnik399.pdf in this repository), that every reduced residue class modulo q contains a prime below q^3.99 for all large q. That bound itself is NOT formally verified here: the paper's zero-location arguments, case analysis and exterior regimes have conventional proofs and computer checks only. (1) The graded near lemma: fix test data (a detector f satisfying Heath-Brown's Condition 1, a Gram test g satisfying his Conditions 1 and 2, a Selberg-sieve weight with heights h_k >= 0 on cells [t_k, t_{k+1}) with t_0 > 1/3 + 2 eps', finitely many nonnegative anchor offsets, a positive lower bound for the weight omega where f is nonzero, and I_B > 0) and eta > 0. For all large q, take a finite family of entries (chi_j, gamma_j, delta_j) of non-principal characters mod q with heights |gamma_j| <= T <= (log q)/3 and a safe anchor at height 2T+1, whose characters are pairwise distinct whenever some sieve height h_k is nonzero (condition (iii) of the paper's Theorem 8.4; without sieve weights a character may repeat, and repeated characters enter through the pair excess e_j). Then the prime-sum responses satisfy (sum_j a_j R_j)_+^2 <= (1+eta) I_B [sum_j (D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j) a_j^2 + (d_1 + eta)(sum_j a_j)^2] for all a_j >= 0. This is a weighted version of Heath-Brown's Lemma 12.1 (1992), which Heath-Brown remarks (section 16, item 9) no neat way of achieving "seems available". Its zero form: the response lemma (a response is bounded below by the zeros it keeps, via the local explicit formula), the threshold form exists tau: sum_j (v_j - tau)_+^2 / D_j <= 1 - tau^2/d with features computed from kept zeros, provided every diagonal numerator D(delta_j) - d_1 + e_j is positive, the entry bounds F(hi - s_j) of the rows, the normalization used by the leaf builders, and the vanishing of the pair excess for separated same-character pairs. (2) The leaf LPs: an exact integer checker for the certificates of the leaf linear programs (bisection trees over threshold boxes, first-order and tangent relaxations with safe rounding, exclusions, weak duality with a free dual) is proved sound: if it accepts a certificate with value v, every feasible point of the LP has objective at most v < 10^16. A bridge lemma turns the threshold form into the LP's near rows. Seven certificates (six leaves of the 3.99 corpus and the program of the large first-zero range) are checked by the kernel (decide +kernel) in the repository (not part of the compared theorems). The analytic part is conditional on four published estimates, stated as explicit hypotheses in the Challenge, each no stronger than its source: Xylouris's Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2 (= Heath-Brown's Lemmas 5.3 and 5.2), Burgess's character-sum bound with k = 3 as printed for primitive characters (Heath-Brown's Lemma 2.1; the form for all non-principal characters is derived), and Graham's asymptotic for Selberg-sieve sums. Mertens' estimate, Abel and partial summation, the Selberg majorant, the decay of Laplace transforms, the finiteness and multiplicities of zeros in a disc, the equality of multiplicities of conjugate zeros for real characters, and all error bookkeeping are proved.
entries.title: Linnik's constant is at most 3.99: A formalization of a weighted version of Heath-Brown's near-density estimate, and of the proof's certificate checker

entries.abstract: For arbitrary finite bidders with heterogeneous finite type spaces, a nonnegative normalized real joint prior, and an interim allocation rule with values in [0,1], a randomized allocation of at most one item realizes the weighted interim masses if and only if every collection of bidder-specific type subsets satisfies Border's union-probability inequality. Weighted feasibility is proved equivalent to conditional feasibility on positive marginal support. Null-type interim values remain unrestricted within [0,1]. For a product of nonnegative normalized distributions, the independent-prior corollary has right side 1 minus the product of the complementary marginal probabilities. Full real-valued sufficiency is proved by finite threshold decomposition and compact convex separation; no sufficiency oracle is assumed.

entries.abstract: Lean formalization accompanying the paper An Exponent of 1.04273 for the Unit Distance Problem by Eric Naslund (cited under sources), which proves the exponent 1.04273 unconditionally with a computer-assisted certificate. Conditional theorem on unit distances in the Euclidean plane. Let B = Q(sqrt 241) and let E be the number field of degree 512 generated over Q by sqrt 241 and square roots of the eight elements -1, -71011068 + 4574225 sqrt 241, (-6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, (6101 - 393 sqrt 241)/2, 31 - 2 sqrt 241, 31 + 2 sqrt 241, 326 - 21 sqrt 241 and 326 + 21 sqrt 241 of B (a basis of the {2,3,5}-units of B modulo squares; E is the maximal elementary abelian 2-extension of B unramified outside 2, 3, 5 and the infinite places). Hypothesis (H) is one displayed numerical inequality for the Dedekind zeta function of E: log(Re zeta_E(1 + 1/300))/512 + (1/300)((L - gamma - log(4 pi))/4 - Re((zeta_E'/zeta_E)(2))/512) < 852/10000, where L = (9/4) log 2 + (1/2) log 3615 and gamma is Euler's constant. The compared theorem proves that (H) implies the existence of finite sets U_j in the plane with |U_j| -> infinity such that the number of unordered pairs of points of U_j at distance one, divided by |U_j|^(10427/10000), tends to infinity. The exponent is exactly 10427/10000 = 1.0427. The conclusion is a sequence statement only; no bound at every sufficiently large cardinality is asserted. The infinite pro-2 tower over B (generators, relation bound, presentation, Golod-Shafarevich infinitude, local data), its retained field and growing Galois fields, the root-discriminant bound, the passage from (H) to the analytic ceiling, the numerical margin and the planar construction are proved in Lean over Mathlib; (H) itself is not proved. Outside Lean, a rigorous computation (certified approximate functional equations for the 255 quadratic Hecke L-functions of E/B and an Euler product with explicit tail) bounds the left side of (H) by 0.0848336; that computation is not part of the formal proof.
entries.title: An Exponent of 1.04273 for the Unit Distance Problem: Lean formalization at exponent 1.0427, conditional on one zeta inequality

entries.abstract: Hordijk and Steel (https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.03919, Section 7, Eq. (21)) conjectured a zero-one threshold for RAF emergence at linear mean catalysis. In the uniform reversible binary-polymer model with split-position reaction identities and food consisting of monomers and dimers, a nontrivial limiting law is established. Each molecule independently catalyzes each reaction, with one catalysis coordinate shared by both directions. If the mean catalysis parameter f(n) satisfies f(n)/n → λ > 0, the probability of a reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) set converges to L(λ). The function L is continuous and nondecreasing, with 0 < L(λ) ≤ 1 − exp(−36λ) < 1. Thus no finite positive threshold separates limiting RAF probability zero from one in this model.
entries.title: A nontrivial critical window for RAF emergence in the binary polymer model

entries.abstract: For any nonempty report type T, any outcome type X, any real-valued valuation v : T -> X -> Real and allocation f : T -> X, DSIC payments exist exactly when every finite closed walk has nonnegative sum of weights l(s,t) = v(t,f(t)) - v(t,f(s)). The proof constructs payments as the infimum of finite path weights from a fixed anchor. Direct edges establish nonemptiness; a return edge supplies an explicit real lower bound before using the infimum's order properties. The payments are zero at the anchor and satisfy every implementing difference inequality. The characterization also holds for arbitrary agents with heterogeneous nonempty report spaces and decidable agent equality, by fixing other reports and assembling anchored slice payments. A three-type example satisfies all two-cycle inequalities but has a negative three-cycle and admits no DSIC payment.

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Gale's top trading cycles algorithm (1974) for the Shapley-Scarf housing market. Finitely many agents (Fin n) each own exactly one house (the endowment is a bijection endow : Fin n ≃ Fin n) and have strict preferences over houses, given most-preferred-first as per-agent permutations rank i : Fin n ≃ Fin n; agent i strictly prefers house a over house b iff (rank i).symm a < (rank i).symm b. The comparator-checked results are TTC.Palomar.ttcTerminates: the TTC procedure (each remaining agent points to the owner of their favourite remaining house, each house points to its owner; each round removes the single directed cycle reachable from a chosen remaining agent, whose members trade and leave) removes every agent within n rounds, since each round deletes at least one nonempty directed cycle from the finite functional pointing graph. This one-cycle-at-a-time form computes the same allocation as the simultaneous version (see the remark in README.md); TTC.Palomar.ttcInCore: the TTC allocation is in the ordinary core, i.e. no coalition S can reallocate its own endowments (Set.BijOn y S (M.endow '' S)) so that every member strictly prefers the deviation; TTC.Palomar.ttcUniqueStrictCore: strict-core uniqueness, i.e. for (x : Fin n → Fin n) with (hxb : Function.Bijective x) and (hx : StrictCore M x) the conclusion is x = ttcAllocation M. This is uniqueness among bijective strict-core allocations (no coalition can weakly block), not a singleton claim about the ordinary core. The library also proves the TTC allocation Pareto optimal (TTC.ttcPareto), individually rational (TTC.ttcIR), in the strict core (TTC.ttcInStrictCore), and strategyproof (TTC.ttcStrategyproof, Roth 1982: no unilateral misreport is profitable); these four are library-only and are not on the comparator surface. The Palomar registry API was searched on 2026-10-01 for "top trading cycles", "housing market", "shapley scarf", "TTC", and "trading cycles" and returned no existing TTC formalization among 397 entries; this is a dated, limited observation, not a universal prior-art claim.

entries.abstract: For a permutation pattern τ, let Av_n(τ) be the set of permutations of length n that avoid τ.  This formalization proves, for every n, that four recurrences from the source paper compute |Av_n(1342)| and |Av_n(12453)|. For 1342 they are the one-threshold recurrence W and the scalar kernel recurrence G, and for 12453 the literal two-threshold recurrence H and the transfer-kernel recurrence G.  These are the cases d = 1 and d = 2 of the paper's counting recurrences for the classes Av(12...d ⊕ 231), the direct sum of an increasing pattern and 231, whose kernel form gives polynomial-time algorithms for every fixed d (the complexity bounds themselves are not formalized).  The counting sequence of Av(1342) has been known since Bóna (1997).  That of Av(12453) was previously known only up to n = 38, from a program of Biers-Ariel that evaluates the recurrence H, and the paper uses its kernel algorithm to compute it up to n = 150 (that computation is not formalized).
entries.title: Counting recurrences for the permutation classes Av(1342) and Av(12453)

entries.abstract: In their study of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola–Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems S′ and S′_T, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension T of Peano arithmetic (PA), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in T, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a T-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's S′ is the case T = PA. More generally, for consistent T ⊇ PA, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when T proves every true Π⁰₁ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable T ⊇ PA by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension T ⊇ PA, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if T is Σ⁰₁-sound and the universal relation otherwise.
entries.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition

entries.abstract:
We formalise the proof of two major recent results on wandering domains of transcendental entire and meromorphic functions: every orbit in a wandering domain accumulates at infinity and at a non-isolated (derived) point of the spherical set of singular values.
Both results are obtained as a special case of a more general theorem, for locally defined functions on possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds. Let f be an open holomorphic function from an open subset O of such a manifold X into X. Different components of O may map to different components of X, even when those source components lie in the same ambient component. Suppose that U is a wandering component of the set of normality of f, and that z is in U. If the orbit of z is contained in a compact subset of X, then it accumulates at a non-isolated point s of the set of singular values. Moreover, this accumulation must occur close to singularities for infinitely many singular values. That is, there exists a sequence (s_n) of distinct singular values converging to s, a sequence of embedded discs D_n containing s and a sequence U_n of components of f^{-1}(D_n), with the following properties. (We say that the orbit of z has "singular encounters"; see HasSingularEncounterSequence in the formalisation.) * the discs D_n shrink to s; that is, every neighbourhood of s contains D_n for sufficiently large n; * each component U_n contains a point of the orbit of z; * s_n is a singular value of the restriction f:U_n\to D_n. In particular, the orbit of z is not contained in any compact subset of O. In the special case of a transcendental entire or meromorphic function, we can take X to be the Riemann sphere, and hence compact, so that the hypotheses are satisfied for any wandering Fatou component.
We also prove a corresponding theorem for measurable wandering subsets of the complement of the domain of normality on which all iterates are defined and injective; here the conclusion is that almost every point of the set (in any chart) behaves as above: ambient escape along a subsequence, or singular encounters.
As corollaries we recover Epstein's absence of wandering domains for finite-type maps on arbitrary open subsets of compact, possibly disconnected complex one-manifolds, and the classical no-wandering results for rational maps, compact-surface self-maps, and class S entire and meromorphic functions.
This is an update from the previous registered submission on Palomar, https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-25-000001&version=3 . The change in this update is to allow functions in the local result to take values in a possibly disconnected complex 1-manifold, rather than a Riemann surface. This aligns the definition with Epstein's original discussion of finite-type analytic maps, which likewise allow (compact) complex 1-manifolds.
entries.title: Absence of bounded-orbit wandering domains

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Myerson's 1981 optimal auction theorem, regular case, in a single-parameter independent-private-values model with real types. Finitely many bidders draw independent types from TypeDist priors: probability measures on ℝ with a continuous monotone CDF and a nonnegative Lebesgue density that vanishes for negative types, so each prior's mass lies on [0, ∞). The formal results are MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.virtualSurplusIdentity: under BIC, the support hypothesis (hsupp : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → 0 < D.F t, i.e. the prior puts positive mass in (0, t] for every t > 0 so zero is in the support), and five integrability hypotheses, the expected payment equals the expected virtual surplus minus the interim utility at the reference type (type zero), expectedPayment p D = expectedVirtualSurplus x D - interimUtility x p 0; and MyersonOptimalAuction.Palomar.optimalAuction: for regular priors (hreg : Regular D, i.e. each bidder's virtual value ψ(t) = t - (1 - F t) / f t is nondecreasing on nonnegative types), the auction that allocates the item to the least-index bidder attaining the highest virtual value whenever that value is strictly positive (no sale otherwise), with envelope payments normalized to zero utility at type zero, is Bayesian incentive compatible and interim individually rational, and raises at least as much expected revenue as any feasible BIC and interim-IR mechanism. Independence is the product measure over type profiles; feasibility is pointwise (∑ i, X i t ≤ 1 for every profile t). Types range over all of ℝ; zero is only the reference/normalization type, never a lowest type. The Bochner integrals defining expectations are totalized, so every expectation claim carries the integrability hypotheses that make it non-vacuous. Ironing for irregular distributions is out of scope. The Palomar registry API searches on 2026-10-01 for "optimal auction", "virtual surplus", and "virtual value" returned no existing Myerson optimal auction formalization ("optimal auction" matched only PALOMAR-2026-10-01-000007, Bulow-Klemperer, a different theorem). These are dated, limited observations, not universal prior-art claims.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Myerson's Optimal Auction Theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Myerson's 1981 revenue equivalence theorem in a single-parameter Bayesian mechanism-design model with continuous real types. The formal result is RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.revenueEquivalence (X P1 P2 : ℝ → ℝ) (h1 : BIC X P1) (h2 : BIC X P2) (hU : interimUtility X P1 0 = interimUtility X P2 0) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : P1 t = P2 t: two Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms with the same interim allocation rule and the same interim utility at the reference type (type zero) charge the same interim payments at every nonnegative type. Types range over all of ℝ; there is no lowest type, and zero is only the normalization point for the payment identity. The envelope lemma RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.envelope_integral and the expected-revenue corollary RevenueEquivalence.Palomar.expectedRevenueEqual are proved alongside; the corollary requires both interim payment rules to be integrable with respect to the prior ((hInt1 : Integrable P1 μ) (hInt2 : Integrable P2 μ)), so its conclusion is an equality of finite expected revenues rather than a vacuous totalized-integral identity. The Palomar registry API search on 2026-10-01 for "revenue equivalence" returned zero entries; the queries "Myerson" and "auction" returned only different theorems (see related_formalizations note). These are dated, limited observations, not universal prior-art claims.
entries.title: revenue-equivalence-lean

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Gleason's theorem in finite dimensions. On a complex Hilbert space of dimension at least 3, every frame function on the orthogonal projections has the form P ↦ Re Tr(ρP) for exactly one density operator ρ. The statement is Kim Morrison's lean-eval problem gleason_theorem_finite, unchanged. The proof follows Cooke, Keane and Moran's elementary proof of Gleason's core lemma for matrices on ℂᴺ, then moves the result to operators by taking matrices in an orthonormal basis.
entries.title: gleason-finite-lean

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Green-Laffont characterization: for finite, nonempty agent and alternative types, efficiency and dominant-strategy incentive compatibility imply that payments have Groves form. The project also verifies four standard properties of the finite VCG mechanism with Clarke pivot payments.
entries.title: vcg-mechanism-lean

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Roberts theorem: for finite nonempty agent and alternative types with at least three alternatives, every onto dominant-strategy incentive compatible choice function is an affine maximizer. The proof follows the modular route: the taxation principle and weak monotonicity, reduction to strong monotonicity by tie-breaking, no-veto-power range analysis, the two-agent affine price representation, and induction on the number of agents.
entries.title: roberts-theorem-lean

entries.abstract: Lean proofs of Yongxi Lin's original weak type (1,1) bounds: c_2 >= 1.6855 and c_2 <= 3.879 for cubes, c_2 <= e for Euclidean discs, and c_n <= (n/2)^(n/(n-2)) for balls in n >= 3. Also proves the classical cube bound c_d <= 2^d.
entries.title: Centred maximal constants for cubes and Euclidean balls

entries.abstract: A Lean proof that a no-reserve second-price auction with one additional independent bidder has at least the expected revenue of the optimal normalized BIC auction under a regular common value distribution.
entries.title: bulow-klemperer-lean

entries.abstract: Asymptotic correctness of the discriminative Kalman filter for a stationary linear Gaussian state model with nonlinear and non-Gaussian observations. Formalizes Appendix B, Theorem 2, Lemma 1, and Remarks 1–4 of Burkhart et al. (2020): weak convergence, eventual Gaussian well-definedness, L1 consistency, the exact Gaussian parameter update, the robust update, and the extension to random input distributions with convergence in probability.
entries.title: Discriminative Kalman Filter Formalized

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of all eleven numbered results and both counterexamples in Local conjugacy in prosolvable groups, arXiv:2609.37678v1. Closed supplements of a pronilpotent normal subgroup are conjugate exactly when locally conjugate under the stated structural hypotheses. Continuous nonabelian cohomology has the stated primary restriction decomposition. Local inclusion and fixed-point results, the GL(2,3) quaternion counterexample, and the order-162 Heisenberg wreath-product counterexample are formalized.
entries.title: Local conjugacy in prosolvable groups

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of von Neumann's 1928 finite two-player zero-sum minimax theorem, a foundation of modern game theory and a cornerstone of mathematical economics. Nash equilibrium existence builds directly on its mixed-strategy solution concept by extending equilibrium existence beyond the two-player zero-sum case; this is historical motivation, not a claimed Lean proof of Nash's theorem. The formal result is Minimax.minimax_theorem {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Nonempty A] [Nonempty B] (u : A → B → ℝ) : maxminValue u = minmaxValue u. The reported Palomar registry API search on 2026-09-29 for "minimax" returned zero entries. The M1 Mathlib survey found no finite zero-sum game specialization in the pinned Mathlib, whose general Sion saddle-point theorem is reused here.
entries.title: minimax-theorem-lean

entries.abstract: Formalization of exact distributional results for the random-permutation greedy maximal-independent-set process on finite trees. For every finite nonempty tree, the complete greedy output law is uniform over maximal independent sets exactly for K1 and K2. For the mixed-spider family T_{k,l}, the development counts maximal independent sets, proves exact output probabilities, and for l=2^k-k proves positive total-variation bias with decay O(sqrt(k)/4^k), equivalently O(sqrt(log n_k)/n_k^2) along n_k=2^k+k+1. The Stage-4 novelty classification is "plausibly new with bounded uncertainty"; no worldwide-priority, global-optimality, matching lower-bound, all-n extremal, or other stronger claim is made.
entries.title: Greedy Uniformity on Trees

entries.abstract: Formalization in Lean 4 of the paper 'A Short Proof of Ball's Plank Theorem' by Arseniy Akopyan and Alexander Polyanskii (arXiv:2609.36163). The paper gives a short proof of Keith Ball's 1991 theorem: if a centrally symmetric convex body in R^d is covered by finitely many planks, the sum of their relative widths with respect to the body is at least 1. The proof is based on a simple proof of a core theorem about linear functionals on R^n and an orthonormal basis. It also yields a short proof of Davenport's problem for centrally symmetric convex bodies (interior-disjointness of a homothet K/(n+1) from n hyperplanes).
entries.title: A Short Proof of Ball's Plank Theorem

entries.abstract: Despons, De Decker and Lacoste (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02366, conjecture following Eq. (33)) proposed that the affinity at maximum production flux is bounded below by the logarithm of the gross amplification ratio in seed-dependent autocatalytic networks. A two-species reversible mass-action counterexample is given by X ⇌ Y with forward/reverse rates (3, 2) and 2Y ⇌ 2X + Y with rates (7, 6). On the positive Y-stationary set, the production current has its unique global maximum at (X, Y) = (1, 1). At this point the exponential of the overall affinity is 7/4, strictly below the gross amplification ratio 2. The network has positive rates, an invertible net stoichiometric matrix, unit production mode and a positive detailed-balance state. The formal theorem establishes the counterexample; the correspondence with the published conjecture is supplied by the witness’s stationary branch and reactant matrix, together with the source’s affinity and chemostat conventions.
entries.title: A two-reaction counterexample to the gross-amplification affinity bound

entries.abstract: Formalization of 18 claims from manuscript Theorems A, B, C, E (extension direction), F, G, H (hierarchy inclusions and characteristic-zero strictness), I, and J. The claims include coalgebraic rounding, algebraic and coalgebraic amenability, Hopf-module quotients, cleft extensions, group and Lie applications, and augmentation-associated graded amenability. Every selected claim is proved without unformalized literature inputs or project-local axioms. Theorem D, the equivalence form of E, and arbitrary-characteristic strictness in H remain in the library but are excluded from the submission.
entries.title: Amenability of Lie, group and Hopf algebras

entries.abstract: There exists a locally finite set Λ in the real line such that the complete complex vector space of tempered distributions locally given by atomic measures on Λ, whose distributional Fourier transforms are also locally atomic on Λ, has Hamel dimension ℵ₀. A countable family gives a unique finite linear expansion of every admissible distribution, and every finite expansion is admissible. The theorem includes the equivalence between a Schwartz-vanishing-ideal definition and the local atomic formulas on both Fourier sides. Temperedness is distributional; no additional polynomial total-variation bound is assumed. This is an exhaustive occurrence result for one constructed carrier, not a classification of arbitrary carriers.
entries.title: A complete crystalline-measure space of countably infinite Hamel dimension

entries.abstract: For the explicit bivector metric induced by diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1) and the Pfaffian cubic on fifteen real coordinates, the joint infinitesimal stabilizer is exactly the uniquely parameterized fifteen-dimensional orthogonal adjoint span. Under the metric condition, ninety specified cubic derivative checks certify preservation at every point. Within the joint stabilizer, commutation with a displayed local Lorentz Hodge operator is equivalent to annihilating its complementary reference and yields a unique six-plus-one decomposition, of dimension seven. Within this fixed-Hodge space, exactly the complementary line acts trivially on all extracted four-plane fields; six specified scalar readings reconstruct the entire visible action. The contribution is the explicit constructive classification and recovery certificates, situated in classical Pfaffian-preserver theory. The metric, cubic and four-plane are supplied data. PDT motivates the construction; selecting a physical coupling is outside these claims.
entries.title: Metric–Pfaffian Stabilizers and Fixed-Hodge Field Recovery

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of the papers arXiv:1907.00405 and arXiv:2107.14616 by Ben Krause and Joris Roos. The result concerns l^p boundedness for a  discrete maximal singular oscillatory operator of Stein-Wainger type, also called a discrete Carleson operator.
entries.title: Formalization of a discrete Carleson theorem of Stein-Wainger type

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation of sharp p-adic extremal behaviour for the restricted binomial gcd G(N;m) = gcd{C(N,k) : 0 < k < N, m divides k}. For every prime p and m >= 2 with p not dividing m, it proves that the maximum of v_p(G(N;m)) over admissible rows is the least r >= 1 with m < p^r, with constructive attainment proved before the least extremal row T is used. It then proves, for every prime p and a >= 2, the exact least-row formula T_p(p^a+1) = p^(3a)+1.
entries.title: Pascal Extremes

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Theorem A: every countable group embeds in a group of type FP_n over the integers for each finite n >= 2. The proof uses a 23-index, 15-triple Fano-plane construction to supply the finite input to geometric, homological, and relative Leary arguments. It does not assert the existence of one FP_infty overgroup.
entries.title: Embedding countable groups into groups of type FP_n

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of J.-H. Evertse, On sums of S-units and linear recurrences (Compositio Math. 53 (1984)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose p-adic Subspace Theorem (Schlickewei's, the paper's Theorem 4) it uses. The library Evertse1984 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 2 (a lower bound for S-integral sums without vanishing subsums, at any set of places), Theorem 1 (finitely many admissible projective solutions of x₀ + ⋯ + xₙ = 0), Corollaries 1 and 2, Lemmas 1 and 2 (polynomial values and shifted polynomial quotients that are S-units), Theorem 3 (for a non-degenerate linear recurrence with at least two characteristic roots, the largest prime ideal norm of u_r / u_s tends to infinity), and Corollaries 3 and 4 (P(u_r) → ∞; u_r = u_s has finitely many solutions r ≠ s). It also compares the paper's cited Theorem 4, the repository's p-adic Subspace Theorem. Fourteen statements are compared.
entries.title: Evertse 1984: sums of S-units and linear recurrences

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the linear independence of 1, ζ(2) and ζ(3) over ℚ. The proof is inspired by A. Fauzan's work on the irrationality of ζ(5) and builds on the Lean formalization of the irrationality of Li₂(1/2), registered in Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-09-30-000013. It shows that the method of that proof can be pushed further. The main difference from the Li₂(1/2) proof is that the rational functions appearing here are allowed to have poles of order two. The remaining details are similar, with some minor modifications. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean.
entries.title: Linear independence of 1, ζ(2), ζ(3) over ℚ

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization proving that the Moh curve parametrized by x=t^6+t^31, y=t^8, z=t^10 is cut out set-theoretically by two explicit equations over every characteristic-zero field. The development computes the polynomial and formal-power-series parametrization kernels, proves the radical equality for the two-generated witness ideal, and proves that the curve ideal has height two and arithmetic rank two, both globally and after completion. It also verifies the exact Hilbert-Burch presentation given by the manuscript's explicit four-by-three matrix.
entries.title: Moh's P3 curve is a set-theoretic complete intersection

entries.abstract: Formal proof of the time-zero Black-Scholes formula for a European call on any strong solution of the geometric Brownian motion SDE, with positive initial price, strike, volatility and maturity, and constant drift and interest rate. The change of measure uses the constant-drift case of the general predictable (dynamic) Girsanov theorem. The discounted stopped asset is a martingale under one fixed terminal measure, and the call-payoff expectation equals the closed-form Black-Scholes expression.
entries.title: Black-Scholes pricing via Girsanov change of measure

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of the automorphism-matching theorems and the quasi-isometry classification of Galton–Watson trees from the paper "The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees" by Jayadev S. Athreya and Sascha Troscheit (arXiv:2609.23882). The audited statements are: the i.i.d. matching theorem on the binary tree (Theorem 5.1), the general Markov matching theorem for typed label processes on the binary tree, in its finite-type and zero-compatible forms (Theorem 6.1), the complete classification, up to quasi-isometry, of Galton–Watson trees with finitely supported offspring law conditioned on infinite diameter (Theorem 1.2), the mutual embeddability theorem (Theorem 1.3), and two-value universality with its quantitative rate (Theorem 1.4). The statements are made in Challenge.lean over Mathlib alone and discharged by Solution.lean from four library targets.
entries.title: The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees: Lean formalisation

entries.abstract: Kosc, Kuperberg, Rajon and Charlat (PNAS 122, e2421274122, 2025, Section 2.1) left open the complexity of detecting an autocatalytic core without a prescribed target species or allowed-food set. For finite reversible reaction networks with literal nonnegative integer reactant and product matrices, this unconstrained detection problem is proved NP-complete. A core is a nonempty entity/reaction pair, minimal under componentwise inclusion, with a selected reactant and product in every selected reaction and a signed real flow that strictly produces every selected entity. The input uses a canonical binary encoding. NP membership and a total polynomial-time many-one reduction from SAT are formalized using Complexitylib’s multi-tape Turing machines, including the Cook–Levin theorem.
entries.title: Unconstrained detection of productive autocatalytic cores is NP-complete

entries.abstract: A Lean-checked proof of the d = 3 case of FKS Problem 2: for every simple graph G on seven vertices, G or its complement has an injective placement in Euclidean three-space under which every edge has length 1. Non-edges are unconstrained and may also have length 1. The full question, for graphs on 2d + 1 vertices in dimension d, is stated and marked open. In the notation of Alon and Kupavskii, the proved case gives f_D(7) ≤ 3; together with the published lower bound it implies f_D(7) = 3. The formal target is the seven-vertex disjunction, not a definition or equality for f_D. The research audience is discrete geometers and extremal graph theorists studying unit-distance representations, graph dimension and distance Ramsey questions.
entries.title: FKS Problem 2 in dimension three

entries.abstract: Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Theorem 5.2 and the following remark) left uniqueness with degradation unresolved for Type II_l cores with l > 2 and, when some degradation rates vanish, for Type V cores. For the source-minimal Type II_l normal forms with l ≥ 3 and the Type V normal forms, unistationarity is established for reversible mass-action kinetics with positive forward and reverse rate constants and arbitrary nonnegative linear degradation. Any two strictly positive stationary concentration vectors coincide, including all internal species of the reversible unit chains. The Type II_l class includes separated stems and the coincident three-fork case. The proof combines passive-chain elimination and a ratio argument for Type V with boundary Jacobian nonsingularity and an implicit-function argument for Type II_l.
entries.title: Unistationarity of Type II_l and Type V normal forms with nonnegative degradation

entries.abstract: An explicit local Hodge operator on the oriented coordinate four-plane 0123, extended by zero, together with the fifteen adjoint basis actions of the orthogonal algebra for diag(1,1,1,-1,1,-1), generates sl(15,K) over every field of characteristic different from two. A finite integral commutator certificate produces signed skew matrix units and one symmetric seed; a general propagation lemma then produces all trace-free matrices. Dimension 224 follows from generation. As a consequence, an endomorphism of this algebra commuting with the commutator actions of the same sixteen generators is scalar, with determinant c^224. The proof includes characteristics three and five without a simplicity assumption. The contribution is this constructive generation-and-rigidity theorem. PDT motivates the chosen operators; assigning a physical response magnitude or gravitational coupling is outside the selected claim.
entries.title: Local Hodge generation of sl(15) and scalar response rigidity

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of a deterministic finite-path necessity theorem for graph-pebbling stackability: a positive-mass nonstackable path configuration above an explicit mass threshold must contain an actual directed integer branch message at most -h.  The package also verifies the exact fixed-total corollary at total n*mu, forcing a message at most -(2*mu-1).  The project's two-sided random path threshold theorem is not part of this Palomar result.
entries.title: ProbStack — Random Stacking on Trees

entries.abstract: The tower theory H is the many-sorted first-order theory of a tower of ZFC universes Z_0, Z_1, ... cut at consecutive inaccessible cardinals, with transition maps j_n identifying Z_n with the rank segment V(kappa_n) of Z_{n+1}.  H is solid in Enayat's sense.  For models M, N, P, with N interpreted in M and P interpreted in N, and an M-definable isomorphism between M and P, there is an M-definable isomorphism between M and N.  The registered statement (Palomar/Challenge.lean) writes out the many-sorted first-order logic of H from scratch, with structures, formulas, satisfaction and definability with parameters.  It states the axioms of H with Separation and Replacement as schemes over all definable classes, finitary interpretations in one-coordinate normal form (each interpreted sort is a definable subset of a single sort modulo a definable equivalence; the reduction from tuple domains is not formalized), presentations, and definable isomorphisms.  The theorem is Theorem 2.1 of the accompanying paper, "Solid idealized Lean", where it is the tower half of the bi-interpretability of an idealized Lean with H.  The proof (Palomar/Solution.lean) reduces the statement to the development's semantic solidity theorem tower_solid.
entries.title: solid-lean

entries.abstract: For all finite subsets X,Y of an abelian group,  |X-Y| <= |X+Y|^λ with λ = (9451e-3286)/(5378e+787) = 1.454277448906…, less than the classical exponent 3/2. A multiscale transfer gives the upper bound (13524e-7359)/(9451e-3286) = 1.312373302115… for the Gyarmati–Hennecart–Ruzsa small-sumset exponent, less than their exponent 4/3. The proof of the first result combines a coupling with distinct differences, entropy inequalities for independent sums, a finite certificate using non-Shannon inequalities, and an explicit limiting certificate. The transfer uses localization and the Plünnecke-Ruzsa inequality over a sequence of scales.
entries.title: Improved sum–difference inequalities in abelian groups

entries.abstract: Johnson's contact criterion for D-stability is expressed as an explicit principal-minor critical-point system. For every real square matrix and every choice of positive barrier weights, D-stability is equivalent to Hurwitz stability and the absence of positive solutions of the associated Fritz-John equations. The proof applies a proper exhaustion of the positive orthant to Johnson's contact variety, so that every nonempty contact set contains a critical point. In dimension five, the criterion is written explicitly as a Lagrange system and a tangency system, with coefficients given by principal minors. Both equivalences are formalized in Lean. The result applies the classical critical-point method to the characterization problem discussed by Kanovei and Logofet (1998) and Kushel (arXiv:2604.16526).
entries.title: A critical-point criterion for D-stability in every dimension

entries.abstract: The computational difficulty of D-stability, raised by Chen, Fan and Yu (1995, doi:10.1016/0167-6911(94)00036-U), is addressed by an explicit integer-matrix reduction from PARTITION. For positive weights of total 2T, the construction produces a matrix of order m + 4 that is D-stable exactly when no subset has weight T. When an equal split exists, some positive diagonal scaling has an eigenvalue with strictly positive real part. A Pell recursion supplies the parameters, with a logarithmic search bound and an explicit bound on every matrix entry. These bounds give polynomial binary output length. Together with the classical NP-completeness of PARTITION, the reduction yields coNP-hardness of D-stability and D-semistability, and NP-hardness of strict D-instability, even for a four-dimensional core with attachments at one coordinate.
entries.title: Deciding D-stability is coNP-hard

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that the 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The value is defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), so zeta2 7 = J(6)/768; the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. ζ₂(3) and ζ₂(5) are known to be irrational, and L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025) proved that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational; the theorem here implies that result and the two registered formalisations of the same maintainer for {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11)} and {ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9)}. An unrefereed draft by C. D. Long claims, by a different method, that ζ₂(s) is irrational for every odd s with 3 ≤ s ≤ 29; it is not used here, and an internal review of it (docs/long_review.md) found a gap in its large-prime step, so we do not regard it as settling the question. No refereed proof that ζ₂(7) is irrational is known to us. The proof uses the linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2−n/2) dt = ρ_n + Z_n ζ₂(7) of the rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} Π_{c∈C_m} (t+1/2+c) / Π_{k=0}^{n} (t+k)^(a_k), with six nested well-poised numerator blocks C_m = [η_m n, (1−η_m) n − 1], η = (5, 7, 7, 9, 11, 13)/40, and pole orders a_k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} that ramp up from both ends; the evaluation at the centred point t + 1/2 − n/2 leaves ζ₂(7) as the only zeta value. The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus, and the size of the coefficients from residue-level Cauchy bounds and a certified maximum of an explicit potential. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by a residue-class analysis of the partial fractions (a class lemma, a kernel identity and per-pole bounds, evaluated on local models of the residue classes whose values are certified in Lean on finitely many intervals) and the prime number theorem, proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem. If ζ₂(7) were rational, the valuations at the auxiliary prime ℓ = 19n/20 − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.
entries.title: The 2-adic zeta value ζ₂(7) is irrational

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Krohn–Rhodes prime decomposition theorem for finite monoids, in a form with aperiodic factors: every finite monoid M divides an iterated wreath product of finite monoids, each of which is aperiodic or a simple group, and every simple group among the factors divides M. The proof follows the local-divisor proof of Diekert, Kufleitner and Steinberg. Unlike the classical statement, the aperiodic factors are not reduced to copies of the three-element flip-flop monoid U₂; for an aperiodic M the statement holds with M as its only factor, and in general it separates the group structure of M, as simple groups dividing M, from aperiodic factors.
entries.title: Krohn–Rhodes decomposition of finite monoids into aperiodic and simple-group factors

entries.abstract: For every integer d ≥ 4, every finite simple graph with fewer than C(d + 2, 2) edges has an injective placement in Euclidean d-space under which every edge has length 1, and the complete graph K_{d+2} has exactly C(d + 2, 2) edges and has no such placement. Equivalently, f(d) = C(d + 2, 2), where f(d) is the least number of edges in a finite simple graph with no unit-distance representation in R^d. Non-edges may also lie at distance 1. Finite simple graphs are represented as SimpleGraph (Fin n), including the empty graph. The proof is Frankl–Kupavskii–Swanepoel Theorem 3, already proved in the GraphDimension library and imported here. The spherical half of the same theorem is not stated. The question belongs to discrete geometry and extremal graph theory, specifically the study of unit-distance representations and the dimension of graphs.
entries.title: Frankl-Kupavskii-Swanepoel Theorem 3: fewer than C(d+2,2) edges embeds in R^d

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the near-linear cycle theorem in "Lovász conjecture holds asymptotically". For every positive ε, sufficiently large connected finite vertex-transitive graphs contain a simple cycle with at least n^(1−ε) edges. The development includes a weaker-constant Bondy–Locke path-to-cycle comparison and the finite approximate-group and expansion arguments used in the path proofs.
entries.title: Near-linear cycles in connected vertex-transitive graphs

entries.abstract: The red-blue pebble game of Hong Jia-Wei and H. T. Kung (STOC 1981) models a computation on a directed acyclic graph run with S words of fast memory and unlimited slow memory: a red pebble on a vertex is its value held in fast memory, a blue pebble its value held in slow memory, and each load or store costs one I/O operation. This formalisation defines the game, complete calculations and the minimum I/O time Q, and proves three families of results from the paper, with explicit constants and, where the paper states one, in its asymptotic form. Q is 0 by convention where no complete calculation exists, so each statement about Q is made only where one does. First, the partition lemma (Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.1): every complete calculation with at most S red pebbles and q I/O operations yields a 2S-partition of the graph into h sets with q <= S h <= q + S, so that Q >= S (P(2S) - 1) wherever a complete calculation exists. Read literally, the paper's Theorem 3.1 is false in two ways, since its rules let inputs be computed free of charge and let inputs be vertices other than the sources; here, as in Elango et al. (2014), the inputs are exactly the sources and cannot be computed. Second, the n-point FFT graph, for n = 2^k with k >= 1: every S-dominator partition has h sets with n (log2 n + 1) <= h S log2(2S) (Theorem 4.1, with a per-set bound sharper than the paper's, which also closes a gap in its proof), a complete calculation exists exactly when S >= 3, and every complete calculation has q >= 2n and n log2 n <= 5 q log2 S (Corollary 4.1 with an explicit constant); Q log S = Omega(n log n) holds with one constant for all such n and all S >= 3, and P_D(S) = Omega(n log n / (S log S)) with one constant for all such n and all S >= 2. Third, matrix multiplication by the ordinary algorithm, for every graph in which the m k n products A_il B_lj are vertices of their own, each with an edge from its two factors, and no vertex can be reached from the products of two different entries of the result; for m, k, n >= 1 this class contains every independent evaluation in the paper's sense. Every complete calculation has m k n <= 2 q sqrt(S) (Corollary 6.2 with an explicit constant), and for k >= 1 also q >= mk + kn + mn; Q sqrt(S) = Omega(m k n) holds with one constant over any collection of such graphs, for every graph of the collection and every S at which that graph has a complete calculation; and for all m, k, n >= 1 some such graph has a complete calculation exactly when S >= 3. Mathlib has no pebble games, so the statements rest on twelve definitions of the formalisation's own, which the Challenge restates for the reader. Not formalised: the paper's upper bounds (its Theorem 2.1 and section 8, which it states without proof), its sections 5 and 7, and its Theorem 6.1 for general expressions.
entries.title: Hong and Kung's red-blue pebble game: the partition lemma and I/O lower bounds for the FFT and matrix multiplication

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the irrationality of Li₂(1/2) = Σ_{n≥1} 2^(-n)/n². The proof is inspired by A. Fauzan's work on the irrationality of ζ(5) and builds on Moritz Firsching's Lean formalization in mo271/Zeta5. The central idea is to establish the irrationality of a real number r by constructing a sequence of integer polynomials P_n whose values P_n(r) decay rapidly as n tends to infinity, while for every rational q, P_n(q) ≠ 0 for infinitely many n. Analytic umbral calculus was used to find suitable polynomials Q_n with rational coefficients. Random matrix theory provides rapid decay of Q_n(r) as n tends to infinity. Estimates of p-adic valuations, together with the prime number theorem, ensure that the values P_n(r) of the corresponding primitive integer polynomials also decay rapidly as n tends to infinity, completing the proof. Similar methods may apply to other values Li₂(1/n), but those cases are not included here. The compared theorem depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the one deliberate hole in Challenge.lean.
entries.title: Irrationality of Li₂(1/2)

entries.abstract: The kissing number of Euclidean 3-space is 12: at most twelve unit balls with disjoint interiors touch a given unit ball, and twelve do. The upper bound follows Musin's extension of the Delsarte linear-programming method. The Delsarte machinery on the sphere (positive-definite zonal kernels up to degree 9 and the LP bound, which by itself gives only 13) is built from scratch, since Mathlib has no spherical harmonics. The lower bound is the cuboctahedron.
entries.title: kissing-number-lean

entries.abstract: García Puente et al. (arXiv:2401.00078v3, Question 3.13) asked whether a unique positive zero-divisor value is necessary or sufficient for absolute concentration robustness (ACR) in at-most-bimolecular mass-action networks. Explicit networks with positive rational rates answer both questions negatively. A further three-species example shows that their candidate algorithm can miss a zero-divisor ACR value under an admissible elimination order, refuting the unrestricted elimination-order form of Conjecture 4.7. For block orders that compare the other species before the distinguished species, completeness is established: every real zero-divisor ACR value is returned when the finite basis consists of nonzero steady-ideal elements whose leading monomials cover the ideal. ACR includes existence of a positive steady state; zero-divisor values include coordinate differences lying in the steady-state ideal.
entries.title: Zero-divisor criteria for absolute concentration robustness

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of B. Adamczewski and Y. Bugeaud, On the complexity of algebraic numbers I. Expansions in integer bases (Ann. of Math. 165 (2007)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights, DiophantineApproximation and ForMathlib, whose Subspace Theorem with algebraic coefficients it uses. The library AdamczewskiBugeaud2007 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 1 (the complexity of an irrational algebraic number in an integer base satisfies p(n)/n → ∞, with (1), p(n) − n → ∞), Theorems 2–4 (automatic and morphic expansions), Theorem 5 in full (β Pisot or Salem, bounded integer digits satisfying Condition (∗)_w: the number lies in ℚ(β) or is transcendental), Lemma 1, Theorems 1A–5A on β-expansions with K. Schmidt's periodicity theorem, and the p-adic Theorems 6 and 1B–4B, together with the finite automata and morphisms of §3, and Theorem 7 in corrected form (u_k < min(b, p)) with Christol's theorem (algebraic ⇒ automatic) and a counterexample to Theorem 7 as printed. The counterexample and the corrected hypothesis were worked out during this formalization, not taken from the cited works (see limitations). Thirty-two statements are compared.
entries.title: Adamczewski–Bugeaud 2007: the complexity of algebraic numbers in integer bases

entries.abstract: Vassena (arXiv:2608.27081v2, Section 8) left open whether sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles with three or more sites admit Hopf bifurcation under mass-action kinetics. For every n >= 3, a componentwise-affine family of positive rate constants is constructed for the n-site cycle with one kinase and one phosphatase and a fixed positive equilibrium. A family of strictly positive, nonconstant periodic orbits bifurcates from this equilibrium, with amplitudes tending to zero and periods tending to a finite positive limit. Each orbit is orbitally asymptotically stable within its compatibility class: sufficiently nearby states with the same kinase, phosphatase and substrate totals have unique positive forward solutions that remain close to the orbit and converge to it.
entries.title: Attracting oscillations in sequential distributive phosphorylation

entries.abstract: Vassena and Stadler (arXiv:2308.11486v3, Supplementary Example D) conjectured that sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles have only unstable-positive cores and that every invertible child-selection matrix has determinant of absolute value one. The determinant assertion is proved, and the restriction to unstable-positive cores is disproved. In the n-site cycle, every child-selection matrix has determinant 0, 1 or -1. For every n >= 3, a six-species child-selection matrix is minimally Hurwitz-unstable and has determinant 1, giving an unstable-negative core. For every n >= 2, there is an unstable-positive core on 2n+1 species, so their sizes are unbounded; every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under every positive column scaling. For every n >= 3, there is also a five-species D-unstable core: a positive column scaling makes it unstable, while every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under all such scalings.
entries.title: Determinants and unstable cores in sequential distributive phosphorylation

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the eight values ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11), ζ(13), ζ(15), ζ(17), ζ(19), ζ(21) of the Riemann zeta function is irrational. The statement uses only Mathlib's riemannZeta, the theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The shortest list of odd zeta values starting at ζ(7) that our literature search found proved to contain an irrational number was ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(35) (W. Zudilin, Math. Notes 2001). The proof uses the very-well-poised linear forms of Zudilin (J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 2004, §8) with five derivatives, 23 factors and the direction vector η₀ = 160, η = (47, 47, 47, 47, 48, 50, 50, 51, 52, …, 66); they are linear forms in 1, ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(21) with rational coefficients. Zudilin anticipated such an improvement but could not prove the asymptotics of his forms (his Lemma 20) for more than three derivatives. The proof here does not need them. The denominators of the coefficients are bounded by Zudilin's arithmetic lemma, the prime number theorem (proved from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem) and a kernel-checked table of 2602 pieces of Zudilin's function φ. For large n the forms are bounded by e^(−748.1n), through a contour integral on a fixed vertical line, pointwise estimates and certified numerical inequalities, without saddle-point analysis. They are non-zero if the eight values are rational, because at the auxiliary primes ℓ = 63n − 1, of which there are infinitely many by Dirichlet's theorem, the constant term has ℓ-adic valuation −5 while the coefficients of the zeta values are ℓ-integral. The theorem does not say which value is irrational. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.
entries.title: At least one of ζ(7), ζ(9), …, ζ(21) is irrational

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof development of reduction idea toward NP-hardness of feature selection for relative Gaussian c-separation in the formulation of Borozan et al. The argument starts from NP-completeness of equal-cardinality partition of positive squares, giving integral Gaussian data via integer roots and an even paired total. Three Gaussians enforce partition balance, and a schedule of d+1 Gaussians enforces binary selectors. Explicit separation of the two blocks makes cross-block hinge penalties vanish. The fixed threshold is (dot s 1 / 2)*d*(d+1)/2 - 3*d/4, an integer multiple of 1/4 for natural input weights. Here d is the full dimension. The main proved result is the pointwise gadget iff. The full complexity reduction is not formalized. The threshold depends only on the input. General Karamata inequality and an unconditional ordinary-PARTITION to perfect-square equal-cardinality partition equivalence are auxiliary results stated in Solution.lean. The square encoding has proved injectivity and numerical size bounds; its NP-completeness argument is documented prose. The original Gaussian gadget predicate also has a proved binary certificate verifier with soundness, completeness, and quadratic work in a bit-cost model. The Gaussian gadget equivalence and square-partition reduction were developed and first presented by the author in this formalization. Their mathematical novelty and priority relative to earlier literature are unknown; no systematic literature search or comparison establishing them has been documented.
entries.title: NP-hardness of Gaussian c-separation

entries.abstract: Lean 4 results (core Lean, no dependencies, no axioms beyond the standard three) about law 1518 of the Equational Theories Project, x = (y ◇ y) ◇ (x ◇ (y ◇ x)). Theorem A: in every magma satisfying 1518 and 3862 (x ◇ x = (x ◇ (x ◇ x)) ◇ x), writing S x = x ◇ x, the set {x, S x, S (S x)} is closed under ◇ with u ◇ v = S v and S (S (S x)) = x; hence every one-generated such magma is the trivial magma or the three-element cyclic shift x ◇ y = y + 1. This proves a classification conjectured by Terence Tao on the Lean Zulip on 2024-11-29 (message 485148288). That message assumed 1518 together with all four of 47, 614, 817 and 3862 and carried no finiteness hypothesis; assuming 3862 alone is no weaker, because Matthew Bolan reported the same day (message 485153888) that 1518 and 3862 already imply the other three. What is added here is a machine-checked proof, not a weaker hypothesis: no proof of the classification was found in the venues searched. Theorem A is what the compared declarations state. Outside them the repository holds an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas that do violate the four targets, with two members checked by kernel evaluation, and kernel-checked certificate identities behind a cohomological obstruction theorem (every 1518-cocycle over the shift with finite fibre is a coboundary), whose reduction is a written proof, and the computations classifying base-dependent extensions of the shift.
entries.title: One-generated (1518 + 3862)-magmas are trivial or the Z/3 shift; an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas violating laws 47, 614, 817, 3862

entries.abstract: A Lean proof resolving the Burr–Erdős–Graham–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 809): for every fixed odd cycle of length at least seven, the maximal anti-Ramsey threshold at floor(n²/4) + 1 edges is n²/8 + o(n²). The seven-cycle case is new to our knowledge. The development proves it and formalizes the stronger full-density result of Bucić, Chen, and Ma for odd cycles of length at least nine.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 809: rainbow odd cycles

entries.abstract: Erdős problem #1219 (erdosproblems.com/1219; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 3, asked by Erdős, Hajnal and Rado): let (n_k) be an increasing sequence of integers such that 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} is strictly increasing and 2^{ℵ_{n_0}} > ℵ_ω; is it true that Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)²?  Shelah (Notes on partition calculus, 1975, §1) proved that the answer is yes.  This project formalizes that proof in Lean 4 with Mathlib: the comparator target erdos_1219 states that for every strictly increasing n : ℕ → ℕ with k ↦ 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) strictly increasing and ℵ_ω < 2 ^ ℵ_(n 0), the binary partition relation PartitionArrow (Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k)) ℵ_ω holds, i.e. every 2-colouring of the 2-element subsets of a set of cardinality Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) has a monochromatic subset of cardinality ℵ_ω (PartitionArrow is the binary case of formal-conjectures' Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel).  The proof follows Shelah's Canonization Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 1.2: the unbalanced Erdős–Rado theorem (2^μ)⁺ → ((2^μ)⁺, μ⁺)² (proved here with a critical-ordinal / closure-point argument), a canonization of the colouring across blocks of sizes (2^{ℵ_{n_k}})⁺ by means of guides generic over all small subsets of the earlier blocks, and Ramsey's theorem for pairs on ℕ.  The target is proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and passes the Lean comparator (landrun sandbox, NanoDa kernel).
entries.title: Erdős Problem #1219 in Lean 4: Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)² (Shelah 1975)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 characterization of two-fold Langford sequences. An m-fold Langford sequence of order l and defect d fills the positions 1, ..., 2ml so that every p in [d, d + l - 1] occupies the endpoints of m pairwise disjoint pairs of positions at distance p. For d, l >= 1 a two-fold sequence exists exactly when 3l >= 2d - 1. For every m, (2m - 1)l >= 2d - 1 is necessary, with l(2d + l + 1) = 0 (mod 4) for odd m, and the bound is attained whenever 2d + l = 2ml + 1; the row of order one exists exactly when d divides m; no three-fold sequence of order 3 and defect 6 exists; and for every m >= 3 the necessary conditions are not sufficient. For every T >= 1, with r = ml mod T, every m-fold sequence satisfies the residue bound r(T - r) <= m * sum |p - T| over p in [d, d + l - 1], which contains the counting bound and the necessity half of the order-one theorem. Every m-fold sequence satisfies the forced-endpoint bound 6mld + ml <= 4d^2 + 2(ml)^2 + ml^2. For every m >= 3 the cell (d, l) = (3m - 3, 3) meets the necessary conditions and admits no m-fold sequence. Equality 2d + l = 2ml + 1 holds exactly when every pair straddles the middle, that is ml < i + s_i for every position i <= ml. Alkasasbeh, Dyer and Howell define these sequences and ask for necessary and sufficient conditions when m >= 2; this repository answers the question for m = 2. Necessity is a distance sum. Sufficiency at m = 2 is strong induction on l: sixteen literal cells, concatenation, and otherwise a mirror-symmetric sequence built by Lemma S from a signed permutation, which is found on the whole cone by inversion, the reversal, a descent along lines of fixed mu, and in the band by 21 block-reversal families plus the two-block reversal tau_l, eight sporadic cells and three bases. The tight line is m interleaved copies of the source's Table 1.
entries.title: Two-fold Langford sequences exist exactly when 3l ≥ 2d − 1; the m-fold counting bound and its attainment, and a residue bound

entries.abstract: We answer the set-theoretic characterization question for digraph support families posed by Mike Steel in Section 4 of Interior operators and their relationship to autocatalytic networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023). A digraph on a finite set E is given by a predecessor map P assigning to each vertex e a set P(e) of in-neighbours, loops allowed, and a set S is supported when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e). The characterization refers only to the family F. Start from the full power set of E with no roots used. A legal step chooses a remaining set S outside F that is inclusion-maximal among the remaining sets outside F, chooses a root r in S that has not been used before and lies in no member of F contained in S, and deletes every remaining set X with r in X and X contained in S. A family F of subsets of E is exactly the support family of some predecessor map on E if and only if some finite sequence of legal steps ends exactly at F.
entries.title: Characterizing digraph support families by rooted-interval deletion

entries.abstract: A formalization in Lean 4 and Mathlib of the Erdős discrepancy theorem, proved by Terence Tao in 2015: for every sequence f(1), f(2), … of signs ±1 and every C there are d ≥ 1 and n with |f(d) + f(2d) + ⋯ + f(nd)| > C, so every ±1 sequence has unbounded discrepancy along homogeneous arithmetic progressions. This is the original ±1 formulation, Corollary 1.2 of Tao's paper; its Hilbert-space-valued Theorem 1.1 is not formalized. The proof follows the architecture of Tao's argument: a Fourier-analytic reduction from a sequence of bounded discrepancy to a stochastic completely multiplicative function with bounded mean-square partial sums; a van der Corput argument, driven by the logarithmically averaged two-point Elliott estimate, forcing such a function to pretend to be a twisted Dirichlet character; and a generalized Borwein–Choi–Coons argument excluding that case. The analytic number theory these steps use is proved in the same development rather than assumed: the entropy-decrement proof of the two-point Elliott estimate from Tao's companion paper, the Matomäki–Radziwiłł short-interval estimate on the major arcs via the Dirichlet-polynomial route of Matomäki, Radziwiłł and Tao, the Halász–Montgomery large-values inequality, a large-values bound for Dirichlet polynomials over primes from a zero-free region of the Riemann zeta function, that zero-free region from Weyl-sum bounds on zeta, and a form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem. Where a published route did not fit, the development adapts it; the adaptations are documented. The theorem depends only on Lean's three standard axioms. This is a formalization of a published result, not a new proof; it was produced by AI agents working through pull requests checked by continuous integration in the ProofFleet repository (formerly MoltResearch).
entries.title: A Lean formalization of the Erdős discrepancy theorem

entries.abstract: Lean proofs of strong duality and exact block composition for the negative-weight adversary bound on total Boolean functions, explicit constant-factor characterizations of bounded-error quantum query complexity in value and Boolean XOR oracle models, and uniform extraction of query algorithms from supplied promise dual certificates. The submission also proves that every output probability of a q-query algorithm on Boolean inputs has a real polynomial representation of degree at most 2q in each model. Seven statements are compared against a standalone Mathlib-only specification of the finite quantum model.
entries.title: Adversary bounds and the polynomial method for quantum queries

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the implication from five explicitly stated literature inputs to a homeomorphism between the ordinary Gromov--Hausdorff space of nonempty compact metric spaces and real square-summable sequences. The proof constructs invariant full-support probability assignments, finite dimensional local models, global AR domination and discrete approximation. The five literature inputs are assumptions, not theorems proved in this snapshot.
entries.title: Conditional Hilbert-space classification of Gromov--Hausdorff space

entries.abstract: Formalization in Lean 4 / mathlib of the existing paper by Furber, Mardare, Panangaden, and Scott, Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (LIPIcs, Vol. 363, CSL 2026, Article 48). This repository formalizes that published mathematics; it does not present the paper's results as new mathematics originating in this repository. Three capstones sit on top of the rest of the paper: Theorem 26 (internal λ-interpretation in SetoidF_A), Corollary 34 (the Engeler model with numerals in V^A), and Theorem 43 (two fair-coin subsets of ℕ that are incomparable under the λ-definable many-one preorder). Domain-theory background is imported from a vendored copy of scott1972. The Palomar Challenge locks Theorem 43 as csl2026 and proposition_36_i on the Engeler graph model. Full Corollary 34 remains kernel-checked in the library and is not represented by a weaker Mathlib-only proxy. Lean is written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott gave the author the paper. This formalization does not claim that the paper's authors participated in it or endorsed it. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake require.
entries.title: Lean Formalization of Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (CSL 2026)

entries.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the multiplicative group K× modulo the field-norm subgroup N_{L/K}(L×) is isomorphic as a topological group to Gal(L/K). The registered declaration is the finite norm-quotient form of local reciprocity proved in the included ClassFieldTheory development. Stronger compatibility, normalization and existence results in that development are documented separately and are not part of the compared declaration.
entries.title: Local class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2

entries.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the idèle class group C_K modulo the image of the idèle-class norm from C_L is isomorphic as a topological multiplicative group to Gal(L/K). The Challenge defines the norm as the determinant on the relative adèle algebra and descends it through principal idèles; the included ClassFieldTheory development supplies the proof of the resulting reciprocity theorem.
entries.title: Global class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2

entries.abstract: Glauberman and Norton (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 119, 1993) end their paper on a combinatorial problem that arises in the proof of the Feit–Thompson odd order theorem with a question of Péterfalvi: can the hypothesis of their Proposition 9 be satisfied for p = 3? The same question is Problem 1 in Appendix C of Bender and Glauberman, Local Analysis for the Odd Order Theorem (1994). Let F be the field with p^q elements, P its additive group, U its group of units of norm one over the prime field, H the semidirect product P ⋊ U, and P₀ the image of the additive group of the prime field in H. Hypothesis (B) asks for an injective homomorphism σ from H into a group G, a finite abelian subgroup Q of G whose order is prime to p, and an element y of Q, such that σ(P₀) normalizes Q and σ(P₀)^y normalizes σ(U). Proposition 9 also assumes condition (A): q does not divide p − 1. This project proves in Lean 4 that the answer is negative: for every prime q with q ∤ 3 − 1, no group G, finite or infinite, satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 3. It also proves Péterfalvi's example from the same paper, which shows that SL(2, 2^q) satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 2, so the hypothesis is not empty. The proof is new. It turns a witness of hypothesis (B) into relations between three copies of the additive group of the field with 3^q elements, and it rules out these relations by arithmetic in that field.
entries.title: Péterfalvi's Problem for p = 3: No Group Satisfies Hypothesis (B)

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Four Color Theorem, ported from Georges Gonthier's Coq proof by Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic's AI model, working as an agent under the direction of Robert D. Barish. The main theorem, FourColor.RealPlane.four_color, states that every simple map of the real plane can be colored with at most four colors so that adjacent regions get different colors. The map may have infinitely many regions, bounded or not; each region must be open and connected, and two regions are adjacent when their closures share a point that lies in the closure of no third region. As in Coq, a compactness argument reduces the theorem to finite maps, which are turned into planar bridgeless hypermaps. A smallest hypermap that cannot be four-colored cannot exist: discharging shows that it would contain one of the 633 configurations of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, and each of these is reducible.
The port differs from the Coq proof in three main ways. Its statement uses Mathlib's real numbers rather than an arbitrary model of Coq's axiomatized reals; the two are equivalent, because all such models are isomorphic and the definitions use only the order. Coq checks that the 633 configurations are reducible with a procedure on trees of colorings, run by its virtual machine. The port replaces it with a new bit-parallel engine whose certificates, generated during the build, are checked by the Lean kernel itself. Finally, the case analysis of the unavoidability proof, written as tactic scripts in Coq, becomes case trees checked by a checker proved correct once. Every computation is carried out by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, and the proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The Four Color Theorem (Lean 4 port of Gonthier's Coq proof)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that the zero-forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph P(n,3) is exactly 8 for every natural number n >= 13. The formalized result is the statement recorded as Conjecture 5 in Arnav Krishnan's July 2026 correction preprint; this repository supplies and kernel-checks a proof of that conjectured statement rather than formalizing a proof already given in the cited preprint.
entries.title: Zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graphs P(n,3)

entries.abstract: In a catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions, a RAF is a nonempty set of reactions whose reactants are produced from the food set by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Steel (arXiv:2305.16714v4, Section 4) asked whether some reaction always lies in at least half of the RAFs. Call a reaction food-ready if all its reactants are food, and abundant if it lies in at least half of the sets in the family formed by the RAFs and the empty set. If some RAF U consists entirely of food-ready reactions, then some reaction of U is abundant, with no condition on the other reactions. If every reaction of the system, except at most two, is food-ready and the system has a RAF, then some reaction is abundant. Finally, the statement that every catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions and a RAF has an abundant reaction is equivalent to Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in the form: every finite union-closed family containing the empty set and a nonempty set has an element lying in at least half of its members.
entries.title: Equivalence of the RAF abundance conjecture and Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of P. Corvaja and U. Zannier, On the rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number: solution of two problems of Mahler and Mendès France (Acta Math. 193 (2004)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose Subspace Theorem it uses. The library CorvajaZannier2004 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms.
